# Bug hunt — running log

Date started: 2026-10-08. Owner: the site's operator. Status: **hunting, not finished**.

Method, in the order the hunt runs:

1. Every automatic detector in the tree: `flutter analyze`, `pnpm --filter @umi/api lint`
   (`--max-warnings 0`), `pnpm --filter @umi/dashboard lint`, both unit suites, and the
   contract tests.
2. Structural sweeps: every route in the generated contract against the permission it
   declares; every request body that no schema validates; every empty catch; every
   `Record<string, unknown>` that reaches a write.
3. A disposable database (`umi_hunt`, built by `docs/migration/build-v3/00_run.sh` plus
   the forward migrations) so the live-DB integration family runs and finds what unit
   tests cannot.
4. The live system: the iMin till on `192.168.1.10`, the local API on `:4001`, the
   dashboard on `:4000`, the database on `:4003`. Real taps, real requests, real rows.
5. When the trail goes cold, the engineering literature (state machines, idempotency,
   RLS, float money, TOCTOU) supplies new lenses, and the hunt resumes with them.

Every finding carries the evidence that proves it, its severity, and the fix. A finding
whose evidence turned out to be an artefact of the hunt's own setup is recorded as
**withdrawn**, with why.

---

### Scope of "restored database", "restored clone" and "the clone" (§137–§144, corrected by §153)

Wherever §137–§144 use those words they mean **the platform database as the platform dump captured it** — the database the
legacy app lived in, and the database this hunt cloned to measure. They do **not** mean the product's world: a database the
chain builds (`umi_local`, the environment table's Local, schema build-v3-79) contains no `core.*` at all, and the current
API code states that the legacy reads are gone (`identity.repository.ts:5-7`, §153.2). Whether the platform database still
carries those schemas today is a one-line check — `select to_regclass('core.people')` — that this workspace cannot make
against Supabase; §153 sets out what is verified and what is not, from the database, the current code and the newest
document, in that order.

## 1. The till could not resume a shift, and the button said nothing useful

**Severity: high (money path, dead end for the operator). Fixed 2026-10-08.**

**Symptom.** The operator pressed "Reanudar turno" on the Centro de caja. The screen
answered with the generic refusal ("No se completó la operación. Intenta de nuevo o
solicita ayuda.") and nothing moved.

**Cause.** The till held a _pending cash command_ (`1df4e4e0-…`) from an earlier attempt
the server had never recorded. Every cash action first asks the server about that pending
command — the guard against posting money twice. The server answered `not_found`, because
a refused cash command runs inside one transaction and rolls back whole, leaving no row
in `merchant.business_command`. The till only cleared the pending record on `succeeded`
or on a non-retryable `failed`; for anything else, and for a different operation than the
one being requested, it threw `CASH_RECOVERY_ACTION_REQUIRED` and refused to send
anything. No screen in the POS clears that state.

**Evidence.**

| Fact                                                                      | Where                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The tap sent only a query, never the command                              | `/tmp/umi-api-dev.log`: repeated `GET /cash/commands/1df4e4e0-…`, no `POST …/resume` |
| The server had no row for that command                                    | `select … from merchant.business_command where command_id='1df4e4e0-…'` → empty      |
| The till clears pending work only on `succeeded` / non-retryable `failed` | `apps/umi-pos/lib/features/cash/cash_controller.dart:1029-1070`                      |
| A failed command rolls back whole                                         | `apps/umi-api/src/modules/integrity/integrity.service.ts:26` (one transaction)       |

**Fix.** `cash_controller.dart`: when the server answers `not_found`, discard the pending
command and continue with fresh ids. A command the server never recorded protects no
money. Covered by `test/cash_center_test.dart` → "a command the server never recorded is
discarded, not carried for ever".

**Verified on the device.** Tap → `POST /cash/shifts/a45f4711-…/resume` → shift version
26 → 27, `suspended_at` cleared, `operator_session_id` repointed to the live session, and
the screen moved on to "Motivo de la diferencia".

**Debt this exposed, not fixed.** The _server_ still has no durable record of a refused
cash command, so nothing else can tell "never landed" from "in flight" except the till's
own record. A failure row written in its own transaction (an outbox) would make the
recovery answer `failed` instead of `not_found`.

## 2. The table-state fixture is not re-runnable, and CI cannot see it

**Severity: medium (test infrastructure; hides real failures on a second run).**

**Symptom.** Running `pnpm test:integration:schema` twice against the same database fails
the second time:

```
FAIL src/modules/table-map/table-state.integration.ts
error: new row for relation "operator_session" violates check constraint "operator_session_end_ck"
   at table-state.integration.ts:370 (the INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE)
```

**Cause.** The fixture's `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` sets `state='active'` and
`expires_at=…` but never clears `ended_at`. The first run ends that session (the spec
exercises locking), leaving `ended_at` set; the second run then writes a row whose
`state` is not `'ended'` while `ended_at` is not null, which
`operator_session_end_ck check ((state='ended') = (ended_at is not null))` refuses.

**Evidence.**

| Fact             | Where                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The leftover row | `runtime.operator_session` `7f3814fb-…-00c6`: `state='ended'`, `ended_at` set                            |
| The constraint   | `docs/migration/build-v3/30_runtime.sql:439`                                                             |
| The fixture      | `apps/umi-api/src/modules/table-map/table-state.integration.ts:365-385`                                  |
| Why CI is green  | `.github/workflows/umi-api-ci.yml`: CI builds a pristine database every run, so the row never pre-exists |

**Fix.** Add `ended_at=null` to the `DO UPDATE` list (and, to be safe, `state='active'`
plus `ended_at=null` in every fixture that re-uses a fixed session id). A fixture whose
whole purpose is idempotence should be run twice by something.

## 3. The documented local reset builds a database the backend cannot run against

**Severity: medium (developer workflow; a fresh local build breaks the till's own paths).**

**Symptom.** `scripts/local-reset.sh --yes` (the documented way to rebuild a local
database) applies `docs/migration/build-v3/00_run.sh` and stops there. That script applies
the numbered root files (`00_foundation` … `99_verify`) and **never** the forward
migrations in `docs/migration/build-v3/migrations/`. The application is written against
the post-migration schema, so the fresh database is missing columns it now uses:
`pos_cart.fired_order_id` (004), `pos_cart.cancellation_reason_code` (007) and the rest.

**Evidence.**

| Fact                                                      | Where                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `00_run.sh` iterates a fixed list of root files           | `docs/migration/build-v3/00_run.sh:8-10`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The reset script never runs the migrations                | `scripts/local-reset.sh` (chain → seeds → contract)                                                                                                                                                                |
| CI does run them, and says why                            | `.github/workflows/umi-api-ci.yml`, "Apply the forward migrations"                                                                                                                                                 |
| Measured: without them, 8 tests fail; with them, 192 pass | `umi_hunt`: `sql-preflight` reported `column "cancellation_reason_code" of relation "pos_cart" does not exist` at `modules/pos-sale/pos-sale.repository.ts:219`; after applying the 11 files, `Test Files 1 failed | 27 passed` |

**Impact in production terms.** A till on a database built this way answers a cancelled
sale with a 500 (`pos-sale.repository.ts:219`) and cannot snapshot a cart that fired to
the kitchen (`pos-cart.repository.ts:777`). The pilot's own database has the columns, so
the site does not show it; a newly provisioned café would.

**Fix.** `local-reset.sh` runs the same loop CI runs, after the chain:
`for f in docs/migration/build-v3/migrations/*.sql; do psql … -f "$f"; done`.

**Withdrawn (was nearly reported as a product bug).** The 8 failures above were first read
as backend bugs. They are an artefact of building the disposable database without the
forward migrations. The CI comment documents the same symptom from the same cause. The
finding that survives is the reset script, not the queries.

**Re-checked 2026-10-09, after the owner's edits to the deploy path.** The reset still stops at the
chain: `scripts/local-reset.sh` runs `00_run.sh` at `:137`/`:165` and then seeds and grants, with no
loop over `docs/migration/build-v3/migrations/*.sql` anywhere in the file. What the owner _did_ add
this round is a mail sink (`deploy/local/compose.yml`'s `mailpit`, documented in the playbook), which
closes the other half of the local workflow — the reset link that §39 found undeliverable. This
finding is intact, and its fix is still the one line §3 asks for: run the loop CI runs, after the chain.

## 4. "The day" is the server's local midnight, not the café's business date

**Severity: low to medium (a control window and every cash report).**

**Finding.** Six places in the legacy cash module build "today" as
`new Date(); dayStart.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)` — the _server process's_ local midnight:

| Where                                     | What it bounds                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cash-write.service.ts:71`                | The per-staff daily top-up limit (`STAFF_DAILY_TOPUP_LIMIT`), a money control |
| `cash-read.service.ts:140`                | Today's stats                                                                 |
| `cash-read.service.ts:169, 176, 179, 215` | Analytics ranges and the weekly window                                        |

**Why it is a defect.** Umi's doctrine is that a café's day is derived from the location's
business date and ends at the configured hour (04:00 by default), never at a server clock.
A VPS that runs UTC — the usual default — puts this midnight at 18:00 in Mazatlán, so the
daily top-up limit resets mid-evening and a cashier can take two "daily" allowances inside
one operational day. The reports have the same offset.

**Evidence.** The six call sites above; the host here runs MST, so the local run hides it
(`date` → `Thu Oct 8 18:13 MST`, `date -u` → `Fri Oct 9 01:13 UTC`); the doctrine is in
`docs/product/UMIPOS_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md` / the cash-center specification (business date is
server-derived, 04:00 rollover); and nothing pins the zone — no `TZ=` in
`apps/umi-api/.env`, in `deploy/pilot/*`, or in `deploy/local/compose.yml`, so the process
takes the host's, which on a VPS is UTC unless someone changes it.

**Fix.** Take the window from the location's business date and its `businessDayStart`, the
way the POS and cash shifts already do, instead of `setHours`. The read models can reuse
the same helper the shift close uses.

## 5. A cash top-up creates stored value with nothing in the cash ledger

**Severity: medium to high (money reconciliation and attribution).**

**Finding.** The legacy stored-value surface is live in umi-api
(`POST /api/:merchantRef/admin/topup`, `/purchase`, `/gift-cards`). Every wallet write
goes through one path, `applyWalletDelta`, which calls
`merchant.append_stored_value_fact(...)` and touches only
`merchant.loyalty_stored_value_ledger`. Nothing in that file mentions
`cash_ledger_entry`, a shift, or a register.

| Path                | Creates                                                  |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `topup`             | Stored value from cash taken at the counter              |
| `gift-cards` (POST) | A gift card whose face value was paid for at the counter |

So when a cashier takes cash for a top-up or sells a gift card:

| Fact                                                                                                             | Consequence                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The drawer's expected cash is built from `merchant.cash_ledger_entry` (`pos-cash.repository.ts`, `expectedCash`) | The cash taken for the top-up is invisible to it                                                  |
| The wallet fact carries no shift or register                                                                     | No way to attribute the cash to a shift or to the operator who took it                            |
| The shift's variance is computed from the same ledger                                                            | The shift closes with a surplus equal to the cash top-ups of that shift, explainable only by hand |

**Evidence.** `cash-write.repository.ts:174-198` (the only write path);
`loyalty_stored_value_ledger` is the only table it appends to; the cash center's
`expectedCash` reads `merchant.cash_ledger_entry` with entry types
`cash_sale | paid_in | paid_out | safe_drop | cash_refund | drawer_correction |
handoff_transfer` — a top-up and a gift-card sale are neither. Both amounts are validated
at the edge (`TopupDto` and `GiftCardCreateDto` require at least $1.00), so this is not a
missing-validation bug; it is a missing leg in the ledger.

**Fix (product, not a one-liner).** Either the till records the cash leg as a
`paid_in`/`cash_sale`-style entry bound to the shift when a top-up is taken in cash, or
the top-up refuses cash and forces an external terminal. The first is the one that keeps
the drawer's arithmetic true.

## 6. The approval boundaries and the routes disagree, and nothing checks

**Severity: medium (a control that exists in the document but not on the wire).**

`config/umipos-pilot-approval-boundaries.json` states 34 boundaries, each naming an acting
permission and the approval permission a _different_ person must hold
(`defaultSelfApproval: false`). The contract marks the routes that actually consume an
approval with `approval: true`. Crossing the two by hand found four actions where no route
with the acting permission carries `approval: true`:

| Boundary                                 | Acting permission             | The route that reaches it                                                                       | Can the request carry an approval?                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manual_terminal_refund`                 | `sale.refund.manual_terminal` | `POST …/tenders/:attemptId/refund`                                                              | **No** — `TenderRefundRequest` = amount, attemptId, commandIdentity, idempotencyKey, locationId, operatorSessionId                                                      |
| `manual_terminal_sensitive_confirmation` | `checkout.terminal.confirm`   | `POST …/checkout/carts/:cartId/terminal-recovery`, `POST …/tenders/:commandIdentity/settlement` | **No** — neither request carries an approval id                                                                                                                         |
| `recount_escalation`                     | `cash.count.submit`           | `POST …/cash/shifts/:shiftId/counts`, `…/counts/cancel`                                         | No, but the close path (`…/close`, `…/variance`) does carry `approval: true`, so the control exists one step later                                                      |
| `reward_approval`                        | `loyalty.reward.authorize`    | `POST …/customer-value/rewards/authorize`                                                       | **Yes** — `RewardAuthorizationRequest` carries `approvalId` **and** `approvalFingerprint`, so the service can verify it while the contract advertises `approval: false` |

Two different defects in one table. The last row is a _contract accuracy_ bug: a client
that trusts `approval: false` calls the route with no approval and gets refused, and a
reader of the contract cannot tell that a PIN will be asked for. The first two rows are the
serious ones: the rule the config states cannot be enforced by the server, because the
request has no field to carry the approval. A single operator holding
`sale.refund.manual_terminal` can give money back at a terminal alone.

**Evidence.** The cross-check script (boundaries × `routes[].approval`), the route
metadata and request models in `packages/contract/generated/contract.json`, and the
service gates: `tender.service.ts:679-691` checks the _permission_ and never an approval;
`pos-customer-value.service.ts:334,347` requires `approvalId` **and**
`approvalFingerprint` where the code does ask.

**Fix.** Bring the three sources into agreement, then check them mechanically — the
repo already has a spec that validates the boundaries file alone
(`apps/umi-api/src/modules/auth/pilot-rbac.spec.ts:234`), so extend it (or add a sibling)
to assert: for every boundary, its acting permission reaches at least one route, and that
route is either `approval: true` or carries an approval field in its request model.

## 7. Prices cross the pesos→centavos line as floats (low)

**Severity: low (a cent can move, on import paths that touch prices).**

**Finding.** Money in this system is integer minor units everywhere it is stored, and two
legacy import paths break that rule when they convert:

| Where                                                               | What it does                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/umi-api/src/modules/conversations/products.repository.ts:389` | `Math.round(Number(v.price) * 100) - p.priceCents` — Zettle gives an absolute price in pesos, the model stores a centavo delta    |
| `apps/umi-api/src/modules/conversations/orders.repository.ts:80`    | `const toCents = (pesos: number) => Math.round(pesos * 100)` — the tool layer's pesos snapshot, which a reorder re-prices against |

`Math.round(x * 100)` is right for the ordinary two-decimal values and wrong for the edges
that arrive from outside: a source value with three decimals (`0.615`), or one whose binary
form sits just under the half (`.005` cases), rounds the wrong way and stores a price a
centavo away from the one the vendor quoted.

**Evidence.** The two call sites; the invariant they break is stated in
`packages/contract/src/*` (`Money.minorUnits`) and followed by the rest of the tree — the
POS parses typed money with `parseMinorUnits` rather than multiplying.

**Fix.** Take the vendor's price as a string and parse it with a decimal-aware parser (the
POS's `parseMinorUnits` is the same rule), instead of `Number(...)` then multiply.

**Checked and NOT a bug.** `mercado-pago-point.transport.ts:521` converts the other way
(`(minorUnits / 100).toFixed(2)`). With an integer in minor units the float error is
~1e-13, orders of magnitude below the rounding step, so the string it sends is exact to
the cent.

## 8. The wallet's daily limits are checked in one transaction and spent in another

**Severity: medium (a control that concurrent requests walk around).**

**Finding.** `CashWriteService.topup` reads the day's totals, decides, and _then_ writes —
and the two halves are separate transactions:

| Step                                                                                     | Transaction                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `topupGuards(...)` — staff sum, card sum, top-ups per card, all `created_at >= dayStart` | `cash-write.repository.ts:137` runs inside its own `withMerchant`     |
| `creditWallet(...)` — the ledger insert                                                  | a second, independent `withMerchant` (`cash-write.repository.ts:202`) |

Two requests that overlap both read a sum under the limit and both write. The staff daily
limit, the per-card daily limit and the three-top-ups-per-card limit are all bypassable
that way, and a double tap or a client retry is enough to try. The guards are the only
thing standing between a cashier and unlimited stored-value creation on that surface.

**Evidence.** `cash-write.service.ts:70-104`; `topupGuards` and `creditWallet` above. The
window itself is also the server's local midnight, already recorded as §4 — the same
`dayStart` is passed straight into these guards.

**Fix.** Check and write inside one transaction, with the lock that serializes the pair:
`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the card row for the per-card limits, and a
`pg_advisory_xact_lock` keyed by `(merchant, staff)` for the staff limit (the ledger has no
row to lock when the first top-up of the day is being created). The limits then hold under
concurrency instead of merely being stated.

The ones sampled by hand are safe — `updatePerson` is only reached with the id `resolveIdentity` just minted for that merchant, `getUserPersonId` uses the authenticated principal's own `sub`, the `conversations/*` pair is the row above — but the guard is a convention, not a structure, and the RLS backstop is off by construction. ## 11. The literature pass: lenses and what each one proved

The instruction is to leave for the engineering literature when the trail goes cold and
come back with new lenses. The trail is not cold yet — two levers are still open — but
three lenses were already in hand and each one paid for itself, so they are recorded with
their sources so the next round starts from them rather than rediscovering them.

| Lens                     | Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | What it checks                                                                                       | Verdict on this tree                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Row security**         | PostgreSQL documentation, _5.9 Row Security Policies_ (`postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html`, published 2026-08-13): a table with no policy is default-deny, and **the table's owner is typically not subject to its policies** | Does every tenant table carry RLS _and_ `FORCE`? Is the owner the app role? Are any policies no-ops? | Closed for `merchant`: 145/145 with RLS and `FORCE`, owner `postgres`. Two restrictive policies with a `true` expression are no-ops beside the permissive isolation policies                                                                                                   |
| **Idempotency**          | Stripe API reference, _Idempotent requests_ (`docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests`): the key is stored with the result, and a retry returns what the first call produced                                                                 | Is the key unique per operation, and is the first result replayed rather than recomputed?            | Held in both money paths: the wallet ledger has a unique index on `(merchant_id, idempotency_key)` and the fact function re-reads on collision, raising a fingerprint conflict if the payload differs; cash commands claim their row inside the same transaction as the effect |
| **Lost update / TOCTOU** | The same Postgres family of rules (an unlocked read-then-write is a race)                                                                                                                                                                    | Does every read-decide-write pair happen inside one transaction with a lock?                         | Holds for the wallet debit (`FOR UPDATE` on the card) and **fails for the wallet's daily limits** — recorded as §8, with the in-house precedent as its fix                                                                                                                     |

### New from the retry lens: the backoff has no jitter (low)

**Severity: low (bounded at three attempts, but the shape is wrong).**

`apps/umi-api/src/jobs/job-options.ts` sets `backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay }` for
every queue and no jitter. When a shared dependency is down — the provider, the database —
every queued job retries at the same offsets (5 s, then 10 s), which is the thundering herd
the backoff exists to avoid. AWS's _Exponential Backoff And Jitter_ names the remedy
(`aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/`: "Full Jitter",
`sleep = random_between(0, min(cap, base * 2 ** attempt))`).

**Fix.** Add a `backoffStrategy` to `workerOptions` that applies full jitter; BullMQ accepts
a custom strategy per worker, so it lands in one place.

**What the same read found and cleared.** The rest of the retry design is careful, not
casual: per-queue attempt counts (`system` gets one attempt, `outbound` keeps the legacy
five), a lock window per queue with the reason written next to it (`turns` needs five
minutes because an LLM turn is a multi-call loop, and the old two-minute reclaim produced
double replies), retention bounds for completed and failed jobs, and `maxStalledCount: 1`
so a job that stalls twice is failed rather than retried for ever.

### New from the contract-invariant lens: the 72-hour replay window does not exist (low)

**Severity: low (contract accuracy; the behaviour that is missing is the stricter one).**

The generated contract names sixteen invariants. One of them, `IdempotencyRetention`,
states: _"A command result replays for 72 hours, then returns IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED"_ — and
the surrounding comment tells a client what that means ("past the window a replay returns
IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED and never a second charge — the client must query the command result
instead").

In the implementation:

| Claim                                      | Reality                                                                                           | Evidence                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| The code `IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED` is returned | It is emitted nowhere in `apps/umi-api/src`                                                       | `rg IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED apps/umi-api/src` → no matches |
| The result replays for 72 hours            | The claim row is written with `expires_at = now() + interval '30 days'`                           | `integrity.repository.ts:46-50`                        |
| Past the window the replay is refused      | Neither `getCommand` nor `result()` reads `expires_at`; a replay always returns the stored result | `integrity.repository.ts:100-120`, `:150+`             |
| A client handles the code                  | No client does — neither the POS nor the dashboard mentions it                                    | `rg IDEMPOTENCY_EXPIRED apps/umi-pos/lib` → no matches |

**Fix.** Pick one and make it true: consult `expires_at` on the replay path and answer the
declared code (the stricter half, and the one that protects a client from treating an
aged-out key as a fresh charge), or correct the invariant and its comment to the retention
the code actually keeps. Either way the check belongs in the integrity spec, which today
asserts the _behaviour_ of a replay but never its window.

### New from the same lens: the offline envelope accepts a sequence the database refuses (low)

**Severity: low (a wrong error class for an input the contract lets through).**

The invariant `OfflineCommandEnvelope` says the sequence _is positive_, and the schema
enforces it: `device_sequence bigint not null check (device_sequence > 0)`, live in the
database as `offline_replay_command_device_sequence_check`. The contract's own model is
looser:

| Layer           | Rule                                                         | Source                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Named invariant | "sequence is positive"                                       | `packages/contract/src/catalog.ts:159`                                                  |
| Database        | `device_sequence > 0`                                        | `docs/migration/build-v3/20_merchant.sql:2092` (and `:2130`), constraint confirmed live |
| Contract model  | `sequence: z.number().int().nonnegative()` — **zero passes** | `packages/contract/src/pos-offline.ts:479`                                              |

So a client that numbers its first command `0` clears validation and is then refused by a
Postgres CHECK, which the API reports as an internal failure rather than a validation
refusal with a field path. This till cannot trigger it — its journal starts at
`nextSequence: 1` with `lastAcknowledgedSequence: 0` (`offline_journal.dart:191-196`) — so
the cost today is a wrong error class for a future or third-party client, and a divergence
between three layers that claim the same rule.

**Fix.** `z.number().int().positive()`, one word, and the refusal becomes what it should be.

### Invariants that hold, verified mechanically

| Invariant                                                                                                 | How it is enforced                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Verdict                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PaymentAmbiguity` — "when status is unknown, `queryOnly` must be true and `canRetryAsNew` must be false" | The contract schema itself refines it: `packages/contract/src/platform.ts:409` and `pos-exception.ts:325` raise a validation error on any payload that breaks the pair, so the API cannot return one                                                                                                                                               | Holds by construction                                         |
| `Money` — integer minor units, uppercase ISO 4217                                                         | `minorUnits` is validated as an integer in the money models; the schema carries `check (currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$')`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Holds                                                         |
| `HardwareSideEffect` — "an unknown physical outcome is never retried blindly"                             | `pilot_hardware_adapters.dart:59-83`: the retry loop re-sends only on `notSent` (the bytes never left) and returns immediately on `unknown`. The policy's `hardwareRetryLimit` bounds _connect_ attempts, not commands                                                                                                                             | Holds in the till, which is where the physical decision lives |
| `KitchenEventOrder` — a client applies only a newer version and recovers a gap from the snapshot          | The POS never applies deltas: the kitchen board re-reads the authoritative query, and a conflict triggers `refresh()` (`kitchen_board_controller.dart:526-592`). `aggregateVersion` is exposed for a delta client that does not exist yet                                                                                                          | Holds by polling; the version rule is unused, not violated    |
| `InventoryLedger` / `LoyaltyLedger` — append-only facts, a projection is never the sole authority         | `stock_ledger_entry` carries the `stock_ledger_append_only` trigger and `inventory_restock_outcome` / `inventory_count_line` / `inventory_reconciliation` / `inventory_command_result` each carry their own; `stock_balance` is documented as a rebuildable projection and no application code writes it (the integration specs assert the grants) | Holds structurally, in the database                           |
| `CustomerPrivacy` — receipt delivery never grants marketing consent                                       | Nothing in the API writes a marketing-consent flag at all (`rg -i marketing_consent apps/umi-api/src` → no matches)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Holds trivially; there is nothing to grant                    |
| `OfflineCommandEnvelope` — fingerprint is SHA-256 hex                                                     | `z.string().regex(/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/)` on the envelope and the command, and the DB repeats it (`offline_replay_command_fingerprint_check`)                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Holds on the fingerprint; the sequence half diverges above    |
| 6 offline-replay + table-order + preflight integration failures                                           | **Withdrawn.** Artefact of a disposable build without the forward migrations (§3)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## 12. The backfilled clone: what it proved and what it found

`~/umi-local-dumps/umi_backfill_v3-20260925T221809Z.dump` is a backfilled build-v3 database
with real rows. Restored into a disposable `umi_backfill_hunt` (5 merchants, the legacy
`core` / `grow` / `loyalty` / `ops` schemas, schema version `build-v3-77`), it turns two
questions from argument into measurement.

### 12.1 Cross-tenant isolation holds, measured

**Verified.** I set a known password on `admin@elgranribera.mx` — a merchant-scoped user
with exactly one membership and no platform role — started a second API instance against
the clone on port 4021, and then asked it for its own merchant's data and for another
merchant's with the same session:

| Route                                                  | Own merchant (`elgranribera`) | Another merchant (`kalalacafe`) |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/merchants/:id/operations?domain=cash_shifts` | **200**                       | **404**                         |
| `GET /api/merchants/:id/settings`                      | **200**                       | **404**                         |
| `GET /api/merchants/:id/cash/stats`                    | 500 (see 12.2)                | **404**                         |
| `GET /api/:merchantRef/admin/stats`                    | 500 (see 12.2)                | **404**                         |

The refusal is a 404, not a 403: the other café is not merely forbidden, it does not
exist for that session, which is the stronger answer. Five real merchants, one session,
no leak.

### 12.2 What the clone cannot answer yet (withdrawn as a bug)

The two 500s are the clone being **behind**, not the code being wrong: they are
`column c.rewards_earned does not exist`, and that column is created by
`docs/migration/build-v3/79_cycle_anchor.sql:69` — a file the pristine chain applies and
the September backfill predates. Applying the later chain files to the clone first is what
the rehearsal does, and is the price of using an old snapshot as a target.

### 12.3 The legacy schemas are writable by `postgres` alone — and umi-cash is postgres

**Severity: medium to high (a security fix that cannot be done the way it is written
down).**

In the clone, `api`, `worker` and `readonly` hold **no** `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` on
any of the 53 tables in `core`, `grow`, `loyalty` and `ops`. Only `postgres` does:

```
postgres -> INSERT  en 53 tablas
postgres -> UPDATE  en 53 tablas
postgres -> DELETE  en 53 tablas
```

`docs/PENDING.md` §1 asks for `REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA core,
grow, loyalty, ops FROM api, worker, readonly` and adds its own warning: _"Verify first
which role umi-cash connects as. If it is postgres, revoking from api/worker does not
restrain it."_ The warning is the finding. `apps/umi-cash/DEPLOYMENT.md` documents its
connection string as `postgresql://postgres:[PASSWORD]@…` in seven places, and the one
route that client still serves (`/api/umi/push-passes`) writes. So the revoke that reads
like the freeze is already true and freezes nothing; the writing role is the superuser.

**Fix.** Give umi-cash its own login role with the grants that route needs (and RLS is not
available to restrain a superuser), then the revoke in `PENDING.md` means what it says and
the legacy schemas are genuinely frozen for every application role.

## 15. The charge screen's "resume the shift and retry" is a silent dead end when the shift is mid-count

**Severity: high (money path). The till cannot take cash and the button the screen
offers does nothing at all. Found 2026-10-08 by driving the real till, after the
operator reported "no puedo reanudar el turno".**

**Symptom, measured on the iMin (`192.168.1.10:5555`), 18:43 local.** One line in the
cart → "Cobrar" → the tender sheet → "Cobrar · MXN 80.00". The server refuses
`409 CASH_SHIFT_REQUIRED`; the surface answers "El cobro no tiene un turno de caja al
cual abonar el efectivo." with one button, **"Reanudar turno y reintentar"**. Pressed
it: **the till sent nothing** — no `GET /cash`, no `POST …/resume`, no
`POST /checkout`. The dialog did not change. Repeated in both states the shift can be
in (operator session dead, operator session live): the same silence.

**Why the charge is refused: the shift is not `open`, because a count was started and
never finished.** The drawer's own rows:

| Fact                                                                                                                                                                   | Where                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Shift `a45f4711-…` is `status='counting'`, `ledger_sequence=8`, register `Caja 1` (`CAJA-1`)                                                                           | `merchant.cash_shift`                            |
| `cash.shift_suspended`, `cash.count_submitted`, `cash.recount_requested` — 2026-10-08 07:00:22Z, 07:03:54Z, 07:04:46Z — and nothing after them for 18 hours            | `merchant.audit_event`                           |
| The one count attempt is `attempt_number=1`, `state='approval_required'`: counted MXN 1,005.00 against MXN 1,205.00 expected, MXN 200.00 short of a MXN 5.00 tolerance | `merchant.cash_count_attempt`                    |
| `requestRecount` is what moved `reconciliation_required → counting` (`pos-cash.repository.ts:876`), and no code path times that state out                              | `merchant.cash_shift`                            |
| A cash tender with no shift id is refused by name                                                                                                                      | `pos-checkout.repository.ts:1204`                |
| The till sends `cashShiftId: null` unless the shift is `open` **and** the session matches **and** `recoveryState == 'none'`                                            | `cash_controller.dart:100-113` (`activeShiftId`) |

**Why the button does nothing.** `_recoverCashShift` (`checkout_surface.dart:3508`)
delegates to `onRecoverCashShift`, which in `catalog_surface.dart:3082` tries three
things and finds no fourth:

| Attempt                    | Test                                                                                                                                                                | Result here                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reclaim an orphaned drawer | `holdState == 'held_by_orphaned_till'`                                                                                                                              | no: the refusal carries `held_by_this_device`                                                               |
| Resume with a PIN          | `cash.canResumePausedShift` (`cash_controller.dart:118`) requires `recoveryState == 'shift_suspended'`                                                              | no: a counting shift reports `reconciliation_required` (session live) or `operator_mismatch` (session dead) |
| Resume silently            | `cash.recoverOwnShift()` (`cash_controller.dart:263`) → `_shouldResumeOwnShift` (`:343`) requires `recoveryState == 'operator_mismatch'` **and** `status == 'open'` | no: the second test fails, it returns `null`                                                                |
| —                          | back in `_recoverCashShift`: `shiftId == null` and `hold == 'held_by_this_device'` → no retry, no pop, no message                                                   | **silence**                                                                                                 |

The last row is the defect: the surface promises a recovery, the recovery answers
"nothing here is mine to fix", and the branch that would at least say so is skipped
for our own drawer. `retryWithCashShift` (`checkout_controller.dart:1004`) would also
have returned early, because it reads `null == null` as "already retried".

The same silence reaches one more status by a second road: the server reports
`handoff_pending` as `recoveryState == 'shift_suspended'`, but `canResumePausedShift`
also demands `status == 'suspended'` (`cash_controller.dart:128`), so a shift waiting
for its incoming operator takes the same dead branch.

**The success path is equally hollow in this state.** From the Centro de caja the
resume _works_ — measured: `POST …/cash/shifts/a45f4711-…/resume → 201`, version
27 → 28, `operator_session_id` repointed to the live session — but `transition()`
(`pos-cash.repository.ts:1955-1959`) keeps the status when it is counting:

```sql
status=CASE WHEN $7='open' AND status IN ('counting','reconciliation_required','closing')
            THEN status ELSE $7 END
```

So the operator resumed the shift, watched the screen move on to "Motivo de la
diferencia", and the very next charge was refused again with the same
`CASH_SHIFT_REQUIRED`. "Reanudar turno y reintentar" cannot deliver what it says while
a count stands, in either direction.

**The fact the screen needed was already in the refusal.**
`deviceRegisterHoldDetails` (`cash-shift-hold.ts:136`) sends `shiftStatus` next to
`holdState`, and `CheckoutState` exposes only the second
(`checkout_controller.dart:75`). The tray drops the field that decides the honest
action.

**Fix, in the order it should land.**

1. `_checkoutError` / `_recoverCashShift` decide by `shiftStatus`, not by the hold
   alone. `open | suspended | handoff_pending` → today's recovery. `counting |
reconciliation_required | closing` → do not promise a retry: say the shift has a
   count in progress and offer one action, "Ir al Centro de caja", because that is
   where a count is finished or cancelled.
2. `_shouldResumeOwnShift` should not require `status == 'open'`: the server's
   `transition()` accepts `counting`, `reconciliation_required` and `closing` as
   sources. A resume there is a session repair, not a return to selling, so it
   belongs with the message in (1) and never behind a "reintentar" that re-sends a
   payload the server will refuse again.
3. Nothing may hold a drawer in `counting` for a whole trading day with no live count.
   Either the count session ages back to `reconciliation_required` (where
   `cancel_count` and `resolve_variance` are both offered), or the till's first load
   says a count is open. Today it is silent for 18 hours and then surfaces as a dead
   button at the moment money is on the counter.

**How to get this drawer back to selling (read from the code; the exit has not been
driven end to end yet).** `submitCount` accepts a shift in `counting` and moves it to
`reconciliation_required` (`pos-cash.repository.ts:751-760,819`). In that status
`countCancellable` turns true when the ledger has not moved and no variance reason or
reconciliation exists (`pos-cash.repository.ts:1769-1776`), the screen shows "Cancelar
conteo", and `cancelCount` puts the shift back to `open` (`pos-cash.repository.ts:976`).
So: Centro de caja → Iniciar reconteo → submit the count → Cancelar conteo. The count
attempt stays in the history as what happened. The other way out is the full close:
register the difference, reconcile, close, and open a fresh shift with the float.

### 15.1 Re-measured on the till, 2026-10-08 20:05–20:11 local (`03:05–03:11Z`) — the operator asked again, and both ends of the loop are now on record

The operator said it a second time ("no puedo reanudar el turno"), so the same shift was
driven end to end with the API's own request log open (`/tmp/umi-api-dev.log`, the `:4001`
`umi_local` instance the till talks to). iMin `192.168.1.10:5555`, `Caja 1`, shift
`a45f4711-cde1-4a7f-b7b1-34e17bde6a13`, `status='counting'`, **open for 27 h 51 min**.

| Step                                                                                                         | What the till sent                     | What came back                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cart `910a8d81` (Burgir pack, MXN 65.00) → `Cobrar` → `Cobrar · MXN 65.00`                                   | `POST /checkout` → `201` (the attempt) | `409 CASH_SHIFT_REQUIRED`, `holdState=held_by_this_device`, `shiftId=a45f4711-…`, `registerId=5aedd2e0-…` (`CAJA-1`); screen: "El cobro no tiene un turno de caja al cual abonar el efectivo." + **"Reanudar turno y reintentar"**                    |
| Press "Reanudar turno y reintentar"                                                                          | **nothing**                            | In the 6 s after the tap the log holds only the 10-second hardware heartbeats (`/hardware/runtime`, `/hardware/commands/remote/claim`). No `POST …/resume`, no `GET /cash`, no second `/checkout`. Screen unchanged.                                  |
| Centro de caja → "Custodia del turno" → **"Reanudar turno"** (bounds `[1197,854][1849,920]`, `enabled=true`) | `POST …/cash/shifts/a45f4711-…/resume` | `cash.shift_open` success, `version 28 → 29`, `operator_session_id` `370076e6` (ended 01:44Z) → `f0bcde80` (live). **`status` stays `counting`.** The Custodia card disappears; the column then offers "Motivo de la diferencia" + "Iniciar reconteo" |

So the two buttons mean different things and neither one resumes a count: the checkout's
button is a silent dead end (§15, re-measured), and the cash centre's button _does_ write —
it repairs the session and hands the operator the close flow. The shift has taken **9**
`cash.shift_open` successes between 2026-10-08 02:14Z and 2026-10-09 01:42Z, and the status
has not left `counting` once. `cancel_count` is the only statement that writes
`status='open'` (`pos-cash.repository.ts:976`) and it demands `reconciliation_required`, so
from `counting` there is no road back to selling except submitting one more count.

**Side measurement, same session — the playbook's seeded PIN does not open this till.**
`docs/development/LOCAL_VERIFICATION_PLAYBOOK.md:26` says "the seeded POS operator PIN is
`1234`". Typed on the till it is refused as `PIN_INVALID` (`merchant.device.pin_failed_attempts`
`0 → 1`), and the screen says "El PIN no es válido para esta sucursal." The keyed lookup
(`posPinLookupHash(secret, merchantId, pin)`) matches `1111 → Cocina KDS` and **`4321 →
Caja 1`**; nothing in `merchant.staff` matches `1234`. The documented PIN is stale for this
base, which is the second way the operator gets stopped before the money screen is even
reached.

### 15.2 The 200.00 the till called short is in the books — checked, because a system-caused "faltante" would be the worst version of this story

The screen in §15.1 said: counted **1 005.00**, expected **1 205.00**, tolerance 5.00, "Faltante ·
Fuera de tolerancia · Pide aprobación". An operator-facing accusation of a shortage is exactly where
a system bug does the most damage, so the numbers are worth auditing rather than accepting. On the
shift `a45f4711-…`, from the live database:

| The drawer's own ledger | Amount                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `opening_float` × 1     | 500.00                                                                             |
| `cash_sale` × 7         | 705.00 — every one received in full (`cash_received = amount`, `change_given = 0`) |
| **Expected**            | **1 205.00** — exactly the figure the screen showed                                |

and the sales behind those entries:

| Check                                                                         | Result                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The seven committed sales on that shift                                       | 50.00 + 115.00 + 80.00 + 50.00 + 130.00 + 100.00 + 180.00 = **705.00**, the same figure the ledger records |
| Duplicate `cart_id` / `receipt_snapshot_id` / `payment_attempt_id` among them | **0 / 0 / 0** — no sale booked twice                                                                       |
| `cash_sale` entries carrying a `sale_id`                                      | **7 of 7** (and the single `opening_float` correctly carries none)                                         |

So nothing in the ledger is unaccounted for and nothing was counted twice: **the 200.00 difference is
real in the books**, and the till was right to demand a reason before closing. That matters for how
the whole story reads — the defect in §15 is not a wrong number, it is that the operator, faced with
a correct demand, was left with a screen that could not act on it: the charge answered
`CASH_SHIFT_REQUIRED`, the resume button sent nothing, and the shift sat in `counting` for eighteen
hours. The arithmetic was the one part doing its job.

The screen's own panel agrees with the ledger, number for number — the §15.1 screenshot reads
`FONDO INICIAL 500.00 · VENTAS EN EFECTIVO 705.00 · INGRESOS 0.00 · RETIROS 0.00 · CAJA FUERTE 0.00 ·
AJUSTES 0.00 · EFECTIVO ESPERADO 1 205.00`, which is the ledger's seven figures rendered without
drift. So of the three layers in this story — the books, the screen and the operator's count — the
first two were right and the third is the one that differed.

### 15.3 The operator asked a third time (2026-10-08 22:1x local): same drawer, now 40 h old, and the count cannot be unwound from the dashboard either

The operator said it again — _"en el pos, no puedo reanudar el turno, a qué se debe"_ — on the same
drawer, and re-reading the rows and the two client gates says the same thing with one new fact
attached. State, read from `umi_local` at 22:16 local:

| Fact                                                     | Value                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Shift `a45f4711-…`                                       | `status='counting'`, `version=29`, `ledger_sequence=8`, opened `2026-10-07 23:19:24Z` (**≈ 42 h**) |
| Register `CAJA-1` (`5aedd2e0-…`)                         | `status='counting'`, `current_shift_id=a45f4711-…`                                                 |
| The one count attempt                                    | attempt 1, `state='approval_required'`, counted 1 005.00 vs 1 205.00 expected (tolerance 5.00)     |
| `cash_variance_resolution` / `cash_reconciliation` on it | **0 rows / 0 rows** — nobody ever recorded a reason or reconciled                                  |
| `operator_session` on the shift (`f0bcde80-…`)           | `state='ended'`, ended `03:41:09Z` (20:41 local) — the till locked it                              |
| So the API's own view                                    | `recoveryState='operator_mismatch'`, `allowedActions=['resume']` — _resume is the only verb_       |

Two client gates close the loop, unchanged by the operator-PIN work now in the tree:
`canResumePausedShift` demands `recoveryState == 'shift_suspended'` **and** the shift's
`status == 'suspended'` (`cash_controller.dart:118-131`) — a counting shift is neither — and the
fallback `_shouldResumeOwnShift` demands `status == 'open'` (`cash_controller.dart:343-356`). So the
charge screen's "Reanudar turno y reintentar" still takes the determinate silence of §15: no request,
no message, the refusal stays. The PIN pad is behind the _other_ branch, so on this drawer it never
appears.

**The new fact.** Every write that can unwind a count is bound to the _terminal that holds the
drawer_: `submitCount` (`pos-cash.repository.ts:742-772`), `cancelCount` (`:929-955`) and
`resolveVariance` (`:1001-1031`) all match on `responsible_operator_id = authorization.operatorId AND
holding_device_id = authorization.deviceId AND operator_session_id = dto.operatorSessionId`. The
dashboard can read the shift and can repair the session (`resume` writes no status change, §15.1), but
it **cannot finish or cancel the count**. §15's advice to send the operator "al Centro de caja" is
therefore half right, and this entry is the correction: the count is finished on the till.

And with every operator session on that device `ended`, not even `resume` can run from anywhere until
the till starts a fresh one with its PIN — which is the first step, not a workaround.

**Exit, in the order it works** (code-verified; still not driven end to end):

1. On the till: operator PIN (the keyed lookup matched `4321 → Caja 1`, §15.1) → **Caja** →
   **Reanudar turno**. This repairs the session; the status stays `counting`.
2. Now `allowedActions` are the count's own — `count`, `resolve_variance`, `reconcile` — and the close
   card offers "Iniciar reconteo" and "Motivo de la diferencia".
3. If the count was mis-keyed: **Iniciar reconteo** → submit → the shift becomes
   `reconciliation_required` → **Cancelar conteo** lights up (the ledger has not moved: count's
   `ledger_sequence` 8 = shift's 8, and no resolution or reconciliation exists) → `status='open'` and
   the drawer sells again. The attempt stays in the history.
4. If the 200.00 is real (the books say it is, §15.2): **Motivo de la diferencia** (it will ask for an
   approval — 200.00 is far outside the 5.00 tolerance) → reconcile → close → open a fresh shift with
   the float that is actually in the drawer.

Severity stays **high**; what changed is the destination of the fix — the terminal, not the dashboard.

### 15.4 The resume re-run as the server's own statement, and the one sentence of §15.3 the code contradicts

The operator asked the same question a third time on 2026-10-09 (_"en el pos, no puedo reanudar el turno, a qué se
debe"_), so the call was taken out of the client's hands and executed as the database's own statement.

**The statement, run verbatim in a transaction that was rolled back.** `transition()`'s UPDATE
(`pos-cash.repository.ts:1953-1985`) against the live row in `umi_local`, with the same nine arguments, wrapped in
`BEGIN; … ROLLBACK;`:

| Argument or result     | Value                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `$7` — the target      | `'open'`, i.e. the resume                                                                 |
| `$8` — the source list | `['open','suspended','handoff_pending','counting','reconciliation_required','closing']`   |
| rows matched           | **1** — the shift is in the source list, so the UPDATE is not refused                     |
| `status` returned      | **`counting`** — the `CASE` keeps it (§15.1 read this from the code; this is it measured) |
| `version`              | 29 → 30                                                                                   |
| `operator_session_id`  | rewritten to the live session                                                             |
| the register row       | `physical_register` `version` 24 → 25, `status` still `counting`                          |

So the `201` is the server's own answer and not a client misreading. Two consequences the code reading did not carry:

1. **The write is a no-op that spends an optimistic-concurrency token.** Any second terminal that loaded register
   `CAJA-1` at version 24 is now refused `STALE_*` by the next legitimate write it attempts, because a resume that
   changed nothing bumped the version anyway. No money moves; somebody else's work is thrown away.
2. **The audit trail records the no-op as a success.** `POST …/cash/shifts/a45f4711-…/resume → 201`, 8 ms, at
   `2026-10-08 23:33:43Z`, `2026-10-09 01:42:21Z` and `2026-10-09 03:11:08Z` (`/tmp/umi-api-dev.log` lines 8204, 10476, 11221) — the same three instants `merchant.audit_event` holds as `cash.shift_open`, `outcome='success'`,
   `public_data={}`. The event name is derived from the target, not from the outcome (`pos-cash.service.ts:415`:
   `eventType: \`cash.shift_${target}\``), so the owner's audit trail of this drawer claims the shift was opened three
times while nothing opened. The fifteen `cash.shift_open`successes before the count (2026-10-08 23:48Z–06:59Z) were
honest: the shift really was`open`, and those are app-restart session repairs. The line between the two is exactly
   the status the verb cannot move.

**The correction.** §15.3 says `submitCount` is bound to the drawer's stored session like `cancelCount` and
`resolveVariance`. Line by line it is not. `submitCount`'s guard (`pos-cash.repository.ts:754-760`) matches
`responsible_operator_id`, `holding_device_id`, `status`, `version` and `ledger_sequence` — **no `operator_session_id`**
— and `requestRecount` (`:877-879`) is the same. Only `cancelCount` (`:936-940`) and `resolveVariance`
(`:1019-1020`) require the shift's stored session to match. The consequence is exact, and it changes the fix: with a
fresh PIN session the till may **take** a count on a drawer whose recorded session is dead, but it may not **cancel**
one.

**Which is why the lying resume is load-bearing.** `resume` is the module's only write that rewrites
`cash_shift.operator_session_id` (the other two assignments are inside open-shift at `:2303` and adoption), and the
server reports `allowedActions: ['resume']` exactly while that session is dead. So the call that lies is also the
till's only door to the count screen: after it, `sessionMatches` is true and `allowedActions` becomes
`['count','resolve_variance','reconcile']` — §15.3's step 2. A fix that only removes `counting` from the resume
sources, the obvious repair, would strand the drawer completely: no `resume` → `sessionMatches` never true → the count
verbs never offered → and `cancelCount` could not run even if they were, because it needs the shift's stored session.
The repair has to move the door, not brick it up.

**And `counting` has no exit to `open` in any layer.** `transitions.counting = ['reconciliation_required','blocked']`
(`cash-domain.ts:162`), pinned by its own spec (`cash-domain.spec.ts:57`: `canTransitionShift('counting','open')` is
`false`). The state is a one-way door whose only handle is _another count_, and the register carries the same status
and the same dead end.

**Fix list, superseding §15's.**

1. Refuse the resume by name when the target state cannot be reached (`INVALID_SHIFT_TRANSITION`, or
   `COUNT_IN_PROGRESS` for the count states), and never write an audit `success` for it. The cheapest correct form is
   the one the domain already states: keep `open`, `suspended` and `handoff_pending` in the resume sources and drop the
   other three.
2. `allowedActions` must depend on the shift's status and not only on the session match, so a `counting` drawer with a
   dead session offers `count` (which does not need that session) instead of nothing but `resume`.
3. Offer `cancel_count` from `counting` under the guards `cancelCount` already proves — the state is a marker left by a
   `requestRecount`, not a fact about money.
4. Guard the audit: write the event only when the returned status is the one the verb claims.

## 74. The refund note the operator types is stored and read by nothing — not even back to the till that typed it

**Severity: low-med (an input that costs the operator effort and informs nobody; it is also the
unfinished half of a request the owner made — "add a note … so the admins see it in the dashboard").
Measured 2026-10-09 00:2x by following the field from the text box to every query that could read it.**

The till's sale-exception screen has a note box:

```dart
// exception_surface.dart:36, :276, :426
final _note = TextEditingController();
…
note: _note.text,
```

and the controller normalises it — a blank note becomes null (`exception_controller.dart:150`). The
API stores it on the preview and on the committed exception
(`pos_exception_preview.note`, `pos_sale_exception.note`, `pos-exception.repository.ts:867`).

Then it stops. The two queries that could show it to a person do not select it:

| Reader                                                                                       | Field list                                                                                                                                         | Note?                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| The dashboard's refunds feed (`dashboard-operations.repository.ts:136-145`, `refunds_voids`) | `exception_type`, `reason_code`, `staff.name`, `approval_id`, totals, `facts` = `{exceptionType, reasonCode, operator, approved, originalReceipt}` | **no**                             |
| The sale's exception history (`pos-exception.repository.ts:1433-1442`)                       | `exceptionType`, `status`, `reason_code`, `amount`, operator, `approvalId`, `receiptReference`, `createdAt`                                        | **no**                             |
| The refunds screen itself (`screens/reembolsos.jsx`)                                         | renders reason code, operator, amount, approval                                                                                                    | **no `note` anywhere in the file** |

So an operator who types _why_ a sale was refunded writes a sentence into the database that no screen
in the platform displays — including the screen that asked for it. The POS's own history of a sale's
exceptions shows type, reason code, amount, operator and approval, and not the text.

**Why it matters more than a missing label.** The refunds screen's own docstring says what it is for:
the owner reviews these acts "for patterns — the 'Por operador' breakdown surfaces refunds/voids
concentrated on one person or booked without a manager approval". The reason _code_ is a category; the
note is the only place the human explanation lives, and the loss-prevention review is precisely the
reader it was collected for. It is also the missing half of the request that produced this field: the
owner wanted the note "for the admins to see in the dashboard", and it is visible nowhere.

**Fix, and it is small.**

1. **One line in the feed**: add `'note', x.note` to the `facts` jsonb in
   `dashboard-operations.repository.ts:140`, and render it in the refunds row (the `detail` string
   already concatenates reason code, operator and "aprobado"; the note belongs in the row's detail or
   its expander).
2. **The same line in the sale's exception history** (`pos-exception.repository.ts:1433`) if the till
   should read back what it was asked to type.
3. **Or delete the input.** A field nobody can read is worse than no field: it asks for care and
   returns nothing, and it makes the record look explained when the explanation is invisible.

**Bound of this evidence:** measured through the code on both ends (the till's input, the API's
writes, and every query that could render it). The live database holds no exceptions yet — §16's
rehearsal is where refunds exist — so there is no screenshot of the empty space; the field lists above
are the proof, and they are exact.

### 74.1 What the note family actually contains — so nobody "fixes" §74 by overwriting a customer

Three different notes exist in this schema, and only one of them is the one the owner asked for:

| Note                                                                        | Where it lives                              | Who writes it                                                                                                                                 | Who shows it                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The **customer's own order note** ("sin cebolla", "soy alérgico a la nuez") | `customer_order.notes`                      | the WhatsApp ordering path (`conversations/orders.repository.ts:134`, `params.customerNote`) and a table order (`table-order.service.ts:282`) | the dashboard's order card renders it (`orders.jsx:517-518`, `order.customer_note`) — **visible, working**    |
| A **line** note ("preparación")                                             | `customer_order_item.notes` (line level)    | the order line                                                                                                                                | the dashboard (`orders.jsx:693-694`) and the kitchen projector (`kitchen-projector.ts:63`, `preparationNote`) |
| The **refund/void** note                                                    | `pos_sale_exception.note` (and its preview) | the till's exception screen                                                                                                                   | **nobody** — §74                                                                                              |

**The note the owner asked for does not exist in the schema at all**: a note an _admin_ adds to a
finished sale, visible in the dashboard. What is closest is `customer_order.notes`, and it belongs to
the customer — which is the trap: implementing the admin note by writing to that column would
**overwrite the customer's own words**, and the allergy note is exactly the kind of text that would be
lost silently. A post-sale admin note needs its own column (and its own renderer in the orders card),
not a reuse of the customer's.

### 74.2 Half of §74 is fixed, in the owner's own working tree — measured, and here is what is left

The receipts screen now renders the note: `recibos.jsx`'s exception rows print `Nota: {ex.note}` when
the field is present (with the comment "until now it reached this screen and stopped"). The data
reaches it — the drawer's rows come from `GET …/sales/:saleId/receipt`, whose exception query already
selects `x.note` (`dashboard-operations.repository.ts:319`, and the row type declares
`note: string | null`). Checking that it was _already_ selected, rather than added in the same change,
is what makes this a one-line fix: the column travelled all the way to the client and only the
renderer was missing.

**Still open, one line each:**

| Reader                                                                                            | State                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The dashboard's **refunds list** (`refunds_voids` feed, `dashboard-operations.repository.ts:140`) | `facts` still carries `{exceptionType, reasonCode, operator, approved, originalReceipt}` and **no `note`** — so `reembolsos.jsx`, the loss-prevention view whose docstring says it exists so the owner can look for patterns, still shows the reason code and not the operator's sentence |
| The **sale's exception history** (`pos-exception.repository.ts:1433-1442`)                        | still selects type, status, reason code, amount, operator, approval and receipt — not `note`, so the till cannot read back what it asked the operator to type                                                                                                                             |
| The **receipts drawer** (`recibos.jsx`)                                                           | **fixed**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

So the note is now visible where it was closest to the data, and still invisible in the two places it
was collected for: the owner's refund review and the operator's own history.
