## 118. The wire vocabulary is two thirds of what the API says: 106 named refusals are renamed at the boundary, and 21 client branches can never fire

**Severity: med-high (a money surface answers with the wrong sentence, and support gets the wrong code).** Found
2026-10-09 by writing the cross-check §53 said was missing — _does every code a client branches on exist on the wire?_ —
which took one script and, as §53 predicted, had never been run.

### 118.1 The mechanism, in six lines

One filter, global (`app.module.ts:141`). Its response builder decides which `code` survives
(`shared/http/all-exceptions.filter.ts:95-103`):

```ts
const explicitCode = 'code' in source && typeof source.code === 'string'
  && API_ERROR_CODES.includes(source.code as ApiError['code']) ? source.code : null;
const code = explicitCode ?? codeForStatus(status);
```

and `codeForStatus` (`:140-148`) is seven lines of fallback: `400 → VALIDATION_FAILED`, `401 →
AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, `403 → PERMISSION_DENIED`, `404 → RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `409 → CONFLICT`, `429 → RATE_LIMITED`,
anything else `INTERNAL_ERROR`. The body is `{ statusCode, error: <that envelope>, requestId, timestamp }` (`:83-90`).

**The filter is right to do this.** The client parses the envelope with the generated schema, and `code` there is
`z.enum(API_ERROR_CODES)` (`packages/contract/src/platform.ts:623`) — a code outside the list would make the till's
parser throw on a refusal, which is worse than a generic code. The defect is not the filter; it is that **the API names
refusals the contract does not declare**.

### 118.2 The census, both directions

Extracting `new *Exception({ code: '…' })` from every non-spec file in `apps/umi-api/src` gives **195 distinct codes**.
Comparing them with `API_ERROR_CODES` (131 values; the generated `contract.json` and `platform.ts` agree value for
value, checked both ways):

| Direction                                                                | Count                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Thrown as HTTP exceptions                                                | 195                                                                                                 |
| … declared in the contract (so the code reaches the client)              | 89                                                                                                  |
| … **not declared, and therefore rewritten** to the status's generic code | **106**                                                                                             |
| Declared but not named at any examined throw site                        | 42 — a **floor**, not a truth: `CASH_SHIFT_REQUIRED` reaches the wire from a helper and is declared |

### 118.3 The cost, measured in the clients that wrote the sentences

The till's refund surface carries a `switch (code)` with a tailored sentence per cause
(`apps/umi-pos/lib/features/exception/exception_surface.dart:719-771`). It names **24 codes; 19 of them cannot arrive**:

```
APPROVAL_EXPIRED            APPROVAL_REUSED             CASH_REFUND_NOT_AVAILABLE
CASH_SHIFT_NOT_ELIGIBLE     INSUFFICIENT_EXPECTED_CASH  ORIGINAL_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND
PERMISSION_REVOKED          REFUND_AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE  REFUND_NOT_ELIGIBLE
REFUND_QUANTITY_EXCEEDS_REMAINING                       REFUND_SELECTION_INVALID
REFUND_TOTAL_INVALID        SALE_EXCEPTION_CONFLICT     SALE_EXCEPTION_CONTEXT_CHANGED
SALE_EXCEPTION_NOT_FOUND    SALE_NOT_FOUND              STALE_PREVIEW
STALE_SALE                  TERMINAL_REFUND_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED
```

(The 5 that do arrive: `APPROVAL_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH`, `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `OPTIMISTIC_VERSION_CONFLICT`,
`PAYMENT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`.) The dashboard names two more that cannot:
`CATEGORY_NAME_TAKEN` (`categories-workspace.jsx:111` — "Ya existe una categoría con ese nombre") and `PIN_INVALID`
(`data.jsx:166`, whose own comment says the POS/operations routes throw it).

So **21 written branches are unreachable**, and each one is a sentence somebody wrote for an operator who will never see
it: a cashier whose drawer has too little for a refund, whose preview went stale, whose sale is not eligible, whose
terminal refund needed confirmation — all of them get the generic fallback, and the surface's own comment says why that
is bad (`:717-718`: the default "keeps the code visible so support can trace it" — support reads `CONFLICT`).

### 118.4 Fix, and the check that finds the next one

For each of the 21, one of two honest moves:

1. **Declare it.** Add the code to `API_ERROR_CODES` with its `retryable` flag — it then travels in both envelopes,
   the client's schema accepts it, and the sentence that already exists starts working. The strongest candidates are the
   ones a client already has copy for.
2. **Stop naming it.** Throw the declared generic code and put the cause in `details`, which the filter _does_ pass
   through for 4xx (`:122-128`) — so `CONFLICT` + `{ reason: 'REFUND_NOT_ELIGIBLE' }` is a legal, parseable refusal,
   and the internal name stays out of the public vocabulary on purpose.

Either way, add the four-line assertion §53 asked for, in both directions: **(a)** every code a client branches on must
be a member of `API_ERROR_CODES` (catches the 21 today); **(b)** every code thrown as an HTTP exception must be either
declared or listed in one place as deliberately internal (catches the 106, and forces the choice). Both are set
differences over two greps — the same shape as §100/§101's vocabulary assertions, on the vocabulary every refusal in the
product travels through.

### 118.5 Measured live: the operator sees "Request failed"

The census above is from reading. One measurement makes it concrete, and it is the _non-destructive_ one — a refusal
path, so nothing is written:

| Step                                                            | Result                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/merchants/:id/catalog/categories`                     | 3 categories, the first named `Pan` |
| `POST …/catalog/categories` with `{"name":"Pan"}` (a duplicate) | `409`, and the wire body is         |

```json
{"statusCode":409,"error":{"code":"CONFLICT","message":"Request failed","retryable":false,
 "correlationId":"51b4766a-…"},"requestId":"51b4766a-…","timestamp":"2026-10-09T06:57:52.108Z"}
```

Two things are wrong in one envelope. The code is `CONFLICT` (the branch at `categories-workspace.jsx:111` is dead), and
the message is the filter's last-resort literal — because the throw site is
`throw new ConflictException({ code: 'CATEGORY_NAME_TAKEN' })` with **no message at all**, and `publicError`'s chain
(`:104-113`) is payload-string → `message` → `error` → `'Request failed'`. Counted across the API: of **459** refusals
that carry a `code`, only **49** carry operator-visible text; **410** carry neither a `message` nor an `error` string
(31 of them carry a `details` bag, which 4xx responses _do_ pass through, so a client could at least read the cause
there).

The screen's own line shows why that lands badly:

```jsx
setError(err.code === 'CATEGORY_NAME_TAKEN' ? t`Ya existe una categoría con ese nombre`
                                            : err.message || t`No se pudo crear`);
```

Both halves fail: the code never arrives, and the Spanish fallback never fires because `'Request failed'` is a truthy
string. The owner reads an English, contentless sentence where the screen has a perfectly good Spanish one in the same
expression. The till is the same story in its own words — its default branch prints the code it was given
(`exception_surface.dart:781-786`: _"Vuelve a intentar. Si el problema sigue, pide apoyo a un gerente. (Código:
$code)"_), so a cashier refused for an ineligible refund is shown **"(Código: CONFLICT)"**, and the support trace the
comment promises points at the status class instead of the cause.

**Fix for the 410.** The catalogue is already generated per code (`errorCatalog`, `catalog.ts:98-106`) and already
carries two facts about each; give it a third — a default operator sentence per code — and let the filter resolve
`message = source.message ?? errorCatalog[code]?.message ?? 'Request failed'`. One generated file then decides what a
refusal _says_, instead of 410 throw sites each deciding not to say anything, and the sentence the client shows stops
depending on which of the two vocabularies the code happened to be in.

## 119. **WITHDRAWN** — `merchant.status='suspended'` and `location.status='closed'` are honoured; what this section claimed was an artefact of my own query and my own grep

> **Corrected 2026-10-09, same day, by measurement.** This section claimed that no request honours `merchant.status` and
> that the catalogue and the checkout ignore `location.status`. **Both claims are false.** The guard's query _does_
> filter on the merchant's status, and the POS's own repositories _do_ filter on the location's:
>
> - `AuthRepository.findMembershipAccess` ends `WHERE t.id = $2::uuid AND t.status = 'active' AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1
FROM grants) OR ${HAS_PLATFORM_GRANT})` (`auth.repository.ts:992-996`). A suspended café resolves to **null** ⇒
>   `MerchantAccessGuard` answers `404 merchant_not_found` and no merchant-scoped request runs.
> - `pos-catalog.repository.ts:32-44` resolves the operator session through `JOIN merchant.location b … AND b.status =
'active'`, and `pos-cart.repository.ts:104-108` opens a cart only `WHERE … b.status='active'`.
>
> **Why I got it wrong, twice, in the same section.** §119.5 measured a query **I had rewritten by hand** — I wrote the
> `grants` CTE and the merchant join myself and dropped the status predicate on the way, then reported the result as "the
> guard's own predicate". And the location half came from a grep for `location.status`/`l.status` that missed the alias
> the code actually uses (`b.status`). Neither error was about the product; both were about the instrument. The
> measurement that corrects it is in §119.5 below, and what survives of the finding is in §136.

**Severity: withdrawn (the residue is low — see §136).** What this section was looking for: the declared codes
`MERCHANT_DISABLED` / `LOCATION_DISABLED`, which are still emitted by nothing.

### 119.1 The promise, in three layers

| Layer        | What it says                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The database | `merchant_status_check`: `status IN ('active','suspended')`. `location_status_check`: `status IN ('active','closed')`. Both columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'`                                   |
| The contract | `API_ERROR_CODES` declares **`MERCHANT_DISABLED`** (`platform.ts:445`) and **`LOCATION_DISABLED`** (`:446`)                                                                                           |
| The code     | those two strings occur **nowhere else in the tree** — no throw site, no test, no client branch. They are the only two of the 42 never-emitted codes (§118.2) whose _feature_ the schema also carries |

### 119.2 Neither flag has a writer, and neither is read where it would matter

**Writers: none.** `merchant.status` is written only where a merchant is created (`merchants.repository.ts:153`) and
`location.status` likewise (`:202`). `rg "SET status='suspended'"` over the API finds shifts and carts, never a café;
the only place a location is ever flipped to `closed` is an integration test (`wallet-carry.integration.ts:169-173`).
So today both flags can only be set by hand in SQL.

**Readers: three, none of them a refusal.**

| Reader                                      | Predicate                                                                     | Effect of a suspension                                 |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/me/merchants` — the dashboard's café list | `merchants.repository.ts:246-248` (`WHERE t.status='active'`)                 | the café **disappears from the switcher**              |
| lifecycle crons                             | `lifecycle.repository.ts:88` (`FROM merchant.merchant WHERE status='active'`) | marketing stops targeting it (correct, and consistent) |
| the dashboard's display line                | `dashboard-operations.repository.ts:34` (`concat_ws(… ,m.status …)`)          | the organization domain prints the word                |

**The request guard does not read it.** `MerchantAccessGuard` resolves access through
`AuthRepository.findMembershipAccess` (`auth.repository.ts:947-962`), whose predicate is
`s.status = 'active'` — the **staff** row's status; the comment beside it is explicit ("A disabled employment grants
nothing, so status is part of the predicate"). The merchant row is joined for `id`, `handle`, `name` and `timezone`
only. No RLS policy closes the gap either: the live catalogue has **0 policies** in `merchant` whose qualifier mentions
`status` (the only `status`-bearing predicate in the RLS file is `platform.tenant_memberships`, the legacy tenancy).

**So a café marked `suspended` keeps selling.** Its sessions stay valid, the catalogue and checkout paths have no
merchant-status predicate, and the single observable effect is that the café is missing from the dashboard's own list —
which also means the operator who suspended it sees the café _vanish_ and no way to tell suspending worked.

### 119.3 The same shape one level down, and this one is half-wired

`location.status='closed'` is honoured by exactly three modules: `table-map.repository.ts:56`, `floor-plan.repository.ts:95`
and `table-order.repository.ts:78` all require `status='active'`. The **catalogue and the checkout do not**, so a closed
sucursal stops showing its floor plan and its table orders while its till keeps selling, taking money and issuing gift
cards. Two modules refusing and two not is worse than none: the operator concludes the switch works.

### 119.4 Fix

1. **Enforce where the request is already resolved.** `findMembershipAccess` gains `AND t.status='active'` — a suspended
   café then answers the existing `404 merchant_not_found`, and the same predicate belongs in the till's device-session
   resolution. Emit the declared codes: a client that _is_ told why (a device already paired, a shift open) should get
   `MERCHANT_DISABLED` / `LOCATION_DISABLED` rather than a bare 404, and the contract already reserves both.
2. **Add the path predicate** in the catalogue and checkout location resolution (`status='active'`), emitting
   `LOCATION_DISABLED`, so the closed-sucursal half stops being half-wired.
3. **Give the flag a writer**, with the audit event every other administrative action carries: the dashboard's `/cafes`
   screen is the natural owner for `merchant.status`, and the location profile for `location.status` (§ the platform
   boundary of §104 is where the permission belongs).
4. **Test it the way it would have been caught**: on a disposable database, suspend a café and a location and assert that
   an authenticated request and a till checkout are both refused, with the declared code. That test is the fix's proof,
   and its absence is why a column and two contract codes have sat unused.

**Stated with its real blast radius:** nothing today can suspend a café _through the product_, so the exposure is not "a
suspension can be bypassed" but "there is no suspension": the only levers an operator has are revoking memberships and
sessions or disabling devices, which are blunter (they also lock out the staff who would fix the problem) and are not
what the contract promises.

> **Correction (§124):** that last paragraph is half wrong, and §124 is the correction. The platform **does** have a
> working, per-request kill switch — the **product entitlement** (`EntitlementGuard`, 61 `@RequireProduct` annotations,
> `umi.effective_entitlement`, `@RequireProduct('pos')` on the till's own controllers). What §119 measures still stands
> as stated — `merchant.merchant.status` is read by nothing and `MERCHANT_DISABLED`/`LOCATION_DISABLED` are emitted by
> nothing — but the conclusion to draw is **"this column is not a second door"**, not "the platform cannot switch a café
> off". The fix for this section is therefore to make `merchant.status` either the same door as the entitlement or
> explicitly not a door, rather than to build suspension from scratch.

### 119.5 **Corrected**: measured both ways, the predicate is the difference

The original text here reported that "the guard's own predicate still answers a real membership" for a suspended café. It
did — for the query I had written, which lacked the status predicate. Run side by side, inside a transaction that was
rolled back (nothing changed; `merchant.status` verified `active` afterwards):

```sql
BEGIN;
UPDATE merchant.merchant SET status='suspended' WHERE id = :merchant;
-- (A) what §119 ran: the CTE + merchant join, WITHOUT the status predicate
WITH grants AS (… s.status = 'active' …) SELECT count(*) FROM merchant.merchant t WHERE t.id = :merchant;
-- (B) the predicate the repository actually carries (auth.repository.ts:994)
WITH grants AS (…) SELECT count(*) FROM merchant.merchant AS t
  WHERE t.id = :merchant AND t.status = 'active';
ROLLBACK;
```

| Query                                               | Rows  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| (A) my simplified version, as §119 ran it           | **1** |
| (B) with `AND t.status = 'active'` — the real query | **0** |

`0` rows is the answer that matters: `findMembershipAccess` returns null, `MerchantAccessGuard` throws
`merchant_not_found`, and a suspended café cannot make a merchant-scoped request at all. The one-row result in (A) is my
own predicate missing, not the guard's behaviour.

## 120. The full count of dead client branches: 23 — and the worst one is the offline replay of a rotated device credential

**Severity: med-high (one of them decides how a till recovers money it took offline).** §118.3 counted the branches by
hand on two surfaces and found 21. This is the mechanised census over both clients, plus the read that says which
branches actually matter.

### 120.1 The method, and its two false-positive modes

Intersect three sets: **(a)** codes the API throws as HTTP exceptions (`new *Exception({ code: '…' })`, specs excluded —
106 values); **(b)** codes `API_ERROR_CODES` does _not_ declare (the filter rewrites those, §118.1); **(c)** codes a
client literal-compares against (`'CODE'` present in `apps/umi-pos/lib` or `apps/umi-dashboard/src`, locales excluded).
The intersection is **25 candidates**, and each was read, because the set alone cannot tell a branch on _the server's_
code from a branch on the client's own identically-named local one:

| Candidate                               | Read result                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HARDWARE_PAYLOAD_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH` | **Withdrawn** — the till throws it itself (`hardware_service.dart:488,498`, `throw StateError(…)`), so the branch is local and reachable |
| `PIN_INVALID`                           | **Withdrawn** — the only occurrence in `data.jsx` is inside the comment that explains the envelope's nesting (`:162`), not a comparison  |
| the other **23**                        | comparisons against a server code, in 15 client files                                                                                    |

### 120.2 The 23, by surface

| Surface                                                                                                             | Codes whose branch cannot fire                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | What the operator gets instead                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Refund / sale exception (`exception_surface.dart`, `sale_lifecycle_controller.dart`, `operator_error_message.dart`) | `APPROVAL_EXPIRED`, `APPROVAL_REUSED`, `CASH_REFUND_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `CASH_SHIFT_NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `ORIGINAL_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND`, `PERMISSION_REVOKED`, `REFUND_NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `REFUND_SELECTION_INVALID`, `SALE_EXCEPTION_CONTEXT_CHANGED`, `SALE_EXCEPTION_NOT_FOUND`, `SALE_NOT_FOUND`, `STALE_PREVIEW`, `TERMINAL_REFUND_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (13) | the refund surface's generic "try again, ask a manager", with `(Código: CONFLICT)` — §118.3                                                     |
| Tender / checkout (`checkout_surface.dart`, `checkout_controller.dart`)                                             | `TERMINAL_BUSY`, `TENDER_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `TENDER_ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `l.checkoutFailed` where three sentences exist for exactly these three causes (`checkout_surface.dart:3093-3095`)                               |
| Offline / device (`replay_engine.dart`, `recovery_actions.dart`)                                                    | `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROTATED`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | a _conflict_ phase and no credential-recovery action — 120.3                                                                                    |
| Cart / entry (`cart_controller.dart`, `catalog_surface.dart`, `entry_controller.dart`, `entry_surface.dart`)        | `CART_NOT_OPEN`, `BRANCH_NOT_FOUND`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | the generic sentence                                                                                                                            |
| Mercado Pago Point (dashboard `device-utils.js`)                                                                    | `MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_ABSENT`, `MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `MP_POINT_STORE_REQUIRED`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | the **permission** sentence (`device-utils.js:180-181`: "Tu usuario no puede administrar los pagos de este negocio") for a _connection_ problem |
| Catalog categories (dashboard `categories-workspace.jsx`)                                                           | `CATEGORY_NAME_TAKEN`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `err.message \|\| t\`No se pudo crear\``— measured live in §118.5: the API sends`"Request failed"`, so the Spanish fallback never fires         |

### 120.3 The worst one, three layers deep

`pos-offline.service.ts:565-571` separates three refusals that a till must react to differently:

```ts
if (!context || context.lifecycle !== 'active')      throw new ForbiddenException({ code: 'DEVICE_REVOKED' });
if (context.credentialVersion !== credentialVersion)  throw new ForbiddenException({ code: 'DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROTATED' });
if (!…permissions.includes('offline.replay'))         throw new ForbiddenException({ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED' });
```

All three are **403**. `DEVICE_REVOKED` is declared, so it survives; `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROTATED` is not, so it arrives as
`PERMISSION_DENIED` — the same code as "this operator may not replay". The till's engine then does the wrong thing, in
the layer where the offline sales are:

| Layer                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                                              | With the code rewritten                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `replay_engine.dart:515-540` (batch submit) | `DEVICE_REVOKED`/`DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROTATED` → `_connectivity.block()` + phase `blockedByDevice` + stop; any other non-transport error → phase `blockedByConflict` + stop | takes the **conflict** branch: connectivity is not blocked, and the engine continues to be re-invocable                                                                                            |
| `recovery_center.dart:590-594`              | `blockedByConflict` renders `l.conflictNeedsAttention`                                                                                                                    | the operator is told the batch **conflicts**, when the device's credential is stale                                                                                                                |
| `recovery_actions.dart:193-198`             | `DEVICE_REVOKED` → `deviceRecovery`; `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROTATED` → **`credentialRecovery`**                                                                               | `credentialRecovery` — the one action written for this cause, and the one that re-enrols the terminal — is **unreachable**; `deviceRecovery` still works, so the screen shows the wrong of the two |

So a terminal whose credential was rotated — the security action that exists to invalidate stolen or replaced hardware —
keeps a queue of offline sales it cannot replay, is told to look for a conflict, is offered a device action instead of
the credential action, and is never stopped from trying. That is the whole cost of §118 concentrated in one branch: the
code inside the server was written to be _acted on_, and the boundary erased it.

### 120.4 Fix

§118.4 covers all 23 at once, but the order matters, and this census supplies it: **declare first the codes that carry a
decision rather than wording** — `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL_ROTATED`, `TERMINAL_BUSY`, `TENDER_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`,
`MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_*`/`MP_POINT_STORE_REQUIRED`, and the refund family — because those branches change what the till
_does_; the purely cosmetic ones can wait for the sentence catalogue. Then add the assertion, which is the only thing
here that is not one-off work: **every code a client branches on must be a member of `API_ERROR_CODES`**, or be declared
local in the file that throws it. That check would have printed these 23 rows on the day it was written, and it is the
same four lines §53 and §118.4 already ask for.

---

## 121. A refusal that comes from the database answers 500: 42 of the 82 codes the schema can raise are mentioned nowhere in the API

**Severity: med-high (a rule refusal becomes a server fault, on the checkout and the hardware path).** Found 2026-10-09
by asking §120's question one layer down — _which codes can the database itself raise, and who translates them?_

### 121.1 The mechanism, and why nothing catches it

A plpgsql `raise exception 'CODE'` inside a query the API ran surfaces at the driver as an ordinary `Error`. Three
things then happen, and none of them is a translation:

1. `IntegrityService.execute` (`integrity.service.ts:17-77`) awaits the operation inside a transaction. A **returned**
   business refusal is recorded (`outcome.ok === false` → `repository.fail(...)` with its code, which `unwrap` later
   turns into an HTTP exception carrying that code) — but a **thrown** error is not intercepted at all: the transaction
   helper rolls back and the error propagates.
2. Repositories that call the functions directly have no `catch` for it — measured: `cash-write.repository.ts` has
   **zero** `catch` blocks, and the call sites are bare `client.query('SELECT merchant.<function>(…)')`
   (`pos-customer-value.repository.ts:1214,1234,1313,1334,1665,1887`, `cash-write.repository.ts:180,307,436`,
   `pos-checkout.repository.ts:1423`, `pos-hardware.repository.ts:707`).
3. `AllExceptionsFilter` sees a non-`HttpException` and answers **500**, with the message replaced by
   "Internal server error" (`:104-113`) and the cause surviving only in the log line (`:63-66`).

So a refusal that the schema itself decided produces the one response a client must treat as "our fault, retry".

### 121.2 The census

Dumping every function body in `merchant`, `runtime`, `umi` and `core` from the live catalogue and extracting
`raise exception '…'` gives **82 distinct codes**. Checking each against the API's non-spec source (any mention — a
mapper table, a comparison, a throw — counts):

|                                  | Count  |
| -------------------------------- | ------ |
| Codes the database can raise     | 82     |
| … mentioned somewhere in the API | 40     |
| … **mentioned nowhere**          | **42** |

The test is generous, so 42 is a **lower bound**: a code mentioned only inside a comment is counted as handled.

### 121.3 Three reachable instances, each with the declared code sitting unused

| Path                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The raise                                                                            | What the client should get                                                                                                               | What it gets |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| Stored-value / gift-card idempotency — `merchant.append_stored_value_fact` / `append_gift_card_fact` raise **`IDEMPOTENCY_FINGERPRINT_CONFLICT`** when a retry carries a different payload (nine bare call sites)               | the function's own `exception when unique_violation` branch                          | **`IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`** — declared in the contract, and both clients map it (`app_error.dart:35-36` puts it in the conflict category) | 500          |
| Checkout — `merchant.commit_customer_value_closeout` raises **`LOYALTY_PREVIEW_STALE`**, **`AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_USED`**, **`STORED_VALUE_ALLOCATION_MISMATCH`**, **`SALE_NOT_COMMITTED`** (`pos-checkout.repository.ts:1423`) | a preview that went stale between read and commit, an authorization already consumed | a refusal with a recovery (re-preview, re-authorize)                                                                                     | 500          |
| Hardware — `merchant.create_hardware_command` and `merchant.assert_hardware_scope` raise **`HARDWARE_PERMISSION_DENIED`** (also `HARDWARE_DISABLED`, `HARDWARE_NOT_ASSIGNED`) (`pos-hardware.repository.ts:707`)                | a till acting outside its hardware scope                                             | a refusal naming the scope                                                                                                               | 500          |

**The first row, measured on real data** (the rehearsal clone has 392 stored-value facts; the call is inside a
transaction that was rolled back, and it writes nothing because it raises):

```sql
SELECT merchant.append_stored_value_fact(<merchant>, <card>, jsonb_build_object(
  'delta',100, 'amountMinorUnits',100, 'reason','topup',
  'idempotencyKey','migrate_cash_card_cmn9hvbyi000x5birme00df37',   -- a real key from that card
  'entryType','loaded', 'currency','MXN', 'direction','credit',
  'commandId','1111…', 'fingerprint', repeat('9',64)));            -- a different payload

ERROR:  IDEMPOTENCY_FINGERPRINT_CONFLICT
CONTEXT:  PL/pgSQL function append_stored_value_fact(uuid,uuid,jsonb) line 33 at RAISE
```

So the raise is reachable with a genuine key, the message _is_ the code (which is exactly how the substring mappers find
theirs — and why a code absent from a mapper is not translated at all), and on this path nobody catches it before the
filter: a till that retries a top-up whose bytes changed gets `500 Internal server error` for the case the contract
declares as `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.

### 121.4 Why the three mapper tables did not catch this — and the blind spot they create for §118 and §120

The API translates database codes with **allowlists matched by substring on the message**:

| Table                                                | Codes | In the contract    | Consequence of the gap                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inventory-errors.ts` (`INVENTORY_CONFLICT_CODES`)   | 19    | **all 19** ✓       | none — the module that took the trouble is the one that is complete                                                                                                |
| `procurement-errors.ts` (`PROCUREMENT_LEDGER_CODES`) | 10    | **7 missing**      | those refusals reach the client as `CONFLICT` + "Request failed" (§118.5); no client branch depends on them (measured)                                             |
| `customer-value-errors.ts` (`CODES`)                 | 16    | **all 16 missing** | every wallet / gift-card / loyalty refusal lands as `CONFLICT`; and the four closeout codes above are not even in this table, so they do not reach a mapper at all |

The instrument lesson matters for the last three sections: a code emitted **from a table** is invisible to a census that
reads _throw sites_ — which is why §118.2's "42 declared but never named" was a floor, and why `NEGATIVE_STOCK_BLOCKED`
(in `INVENTORY_CONFLICT_CODES`, declared, and branched on by the till) was never at risk. The residue on the client side
of this whole direction is one branch: the POS's central operator-message table names `GIFT_CARD_NOT_FOUND`
(`operator_error_message.dart`), which the customer-value table can emit but the contract does not declare.

### 121.5 Fix

1. **Cover each module's own raises.** For every module, the set of codes its mapper can produce must equal the set of
   codes the functions it calls can raise. That is a query over `pg_proc` (the same one this section ran) plus the
   mapper table — and it is the check that would have found all 42.
2. **Translate anything unmapped into a declared code.** The catch belongs where the query is issued: an unknown
   `raise exception` from a ledger or command function is a **rule refusal**, not a fault, so it should map to a
   declared code (`CONFLICT`/`IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`) with the raw code in `details`, which the filter passes through for
   4xx (§118.4). A truly internal invariant — a scope guard that means the API set its own context wrong — can stay a
   500, but by decision and by list, not by omission.
3. **Then the two-direction assertion** of §118.4/§120.4, in the form this section supplies: _every code a plpgsql
   function the API calls can raise is either mapped to a declared code or listed once as deliberately internal._

### 121.6 How many of the 42 a request can actually hit: 33

"Unmentioned in the API" is not the same as "unreachable", so each of the 42 was traced through three channels: the
**function that raises it** → is that function named in API source? → if not, does some function the API _does_ name
call it? (→ and, third, could a trigger raise it on a write, which no call-site census sees).

| Channel                                                                                               | Codes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Examples                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Raised by a function the API calls directly                                                           | **22**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `IDEMPOTENCY_FINGERPRINT_CONFLICT` (`append_stored_value_fact`/`append_gift_card_fact`, 9 call sites), the `commit_customer_value_closeout` family (`LOYALTY_PREVIEW_STALE`, `AUTHORIZATION_ALREADY_USED`, `STORED_VALUE_ALLOCATION_MISMATCH`, `SALE_NOT_COMMITTED`, `STORED_VALUE_FINGERPRINT_CONFLICT`, `WALLET_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED`, `CUSTOMER_VALUE_SALE_REQUIRED`), `HARDWARE_PERMISSION_DENIED` / `HARDWARE_NOT_ASSIGNED` / … through `create_hardware_command`, `VALUE_REVERSAL_EXCEEDS_ORIGINAL` through `reverse_customer_value`, `RESERVATION_RELEASE_TYPE_INVALID`, `INVENTORY_LOT_SCOPE`, `COUNT_CORRECTION_DIRECTION_REQUIRED`, the `LOYALTY_*` preview pair |
| Raised by a function that a **function the API calls** calls                                          | **11**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | the four customer-value scope guards (`CUSTOMER_VALUE_{CONTEXT,DEVICE_CONTEXT,DEVICE_SCOPE,MERCHANT_SCOPE}_REQUIRED`) — reachable from **ten** API-called functions, i.e. from every customer-value write; `GIFT_CARD_ACTIVATION_CONFLICT` and `GIFT_CARD_FUNDING_AMOUNT_MISMATCH` through `commit_customer_value_closeout` → the **checkout**; `HARDWARE_CONFIGURATION_INVALID`, `HARDWARE_ENTITLEMENT_DISABLED`, `HARDWARE_NETWORK_ENDPOINT_INVALID`, `HARDWARE_OPERATOR_SESSION_REQUIRED` through the hardware functions; `EXPIRY_BATCH_INVALID` through the expiry worker                                                                                           |
| **Total reachable from a request**                                                                    | **33**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | each one answers `500 Internal server error` where a refusal belongs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| No traced caller at any depth (BFS over the call graph, four hops from every API-referenced function) | **9** — and most are **trigger** functions, where a 500 is arguably the honest answer: `HARDWARE_FACT_IMMUTABLE` (`hardware_immutable`, an append-only guard), `STORED_VALUE_PROJECTION_MISSING` and `GIFT_CARD_PROJECTION_MISSING` (`project_customer_value_fact`, the projection trigger — §117), `TABLE_STATE_TURN_TIMER_RESTART` (checked by hand, withdrawn below), plus `INVENTORY_BALANCE_NOT_FOUND`, `INVENTORY_MODIFIER_SCOPE`, `STORED_VALUE_ACCOUNT_SCOPE`, `STORED_VALUE_ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE`, `GIFT_CARD_ACCOUNT_SCOPE` |

**The third channel, checked by hand for its one instance.** `TABLE_STATE_TURN_TIMER_RESTART` is raised by the trigger
`table_state_turn_timer_immutable` on `merchant.table_state` — whenever a row that already had `seated_at` gets a
different one ("the turn timer restarted"). A trigger needs no call site, so the census cannot see it, and it fires on
the till's own seating path. Read against the two writers: `seat` pre-checks `current?.seated_at` and _also_ guards its
upsert with `WHERE merchant.table_state.seated_at IS NULL` (`table-map.repository.ts:233,246`), and the move path
requires the source seated and the destination free (`:275-293`) — so the trigger's condition is one the API's own guards
make **unreachable**, and this instance is withdrawn. Recorded because the channel is real: a trigger would have been
invisible to every count above, and the sweep that fixes §121 has to include trigger functions, not only the functions
the API names.

## 122. The census's fourth blind spot: a code built by an expression — and the Mercado Pago refusal that answers "try again" for a refusal a retry cannot change

**Severity: med (a permanent vendor refusal is presented as retryable, and the fact that would fix it is already in the
payload).** Found 2026-10-09 by checking the Devices screen against its payloads, which is where the sheet lives.

### 122.1 The instance

`PointTerminalService.translate` builds its refusal code with a **ternary** (`point-terminal.service.ts:486-490`):

```ts
return new ConflictException({
  code: operation === 'store' ? 'MP_POINT_STORE_REFUSED' : 'MP_POINT_TERMINAL_SETUP_FAILED',
  details: { vendorCode: error.code, status: error.status },
});
```

Neither of those two codes is declared by the contract (checked), so the filter rewrites both to `CONFLICT` — and neither
appeared in §120's census, nor in §121's, because both were extracted by matching `code: 'LITERAL'`, a shape this call
site does not have. **That is the fourth blind spot of the same instrument**, after §117.8's in-file accessor, §121.4's
mapper tables, and now expressions: §120's count of 23 dead client branches is a **floor**, not a total.

### 122.2 What the operator sees, and what the payload already knows

The store sheet has five specific sentences and a fallback (`device-utils.js:164-181`): `MP_POINT_STORE_REFUSED`,
`MP_POINT_STORE_REQUIRED`, `MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_ABSENT`, `MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, then
_"No se pudo crear la tienda. Intenta de nuevo."_ With the code rewritten:

| Branch                                                                                  | Arrives?                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MP_POINT_STORE_REFUSED`                                                                | no — rewritten to `CONFLICT`, and this is exactly the case that happens |
| `MP_POINT_STORE_REQUIRED`, `MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_ABSENT`, `MP_POINT_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED` | no — §120's three                                                       |
| `PERMISSION_DENIED`                                                                     | only when the _user_ lacks the permission, which is not this refusal    |
| the fallback                                                                            | **always**, for a refused address                                       |

So the answer to "Mercado Pago rejected this business address" is **"try again"** — advice that cannot work, since the
same address will be refused the same way. And the actionable half is _in the same envelope_: the service attaches
`details: { vendorCode, status }` in all four of its branches (`:465,475,481,489`), the filter passes `details` through
for 4xx (§118.4), `mpPointStoreRefusalCode` unwraps it correctly (`device-utils.js:150-156`, whose comment spells out the
`err.details.error.details` nesting), and the sheet renders it — as a **raw mono token** next to that sentence
(`devices.jsx:2682,2867-2871`: `invalid_city` in `var(--font-mono)`). The screen has the fact and no sentence for it.

### 122.3 Fix — and this one closes the whole arc

1. **Declare the two codes** (they are the vocabulary of a vendor refusal the operator must act on) and let
   `mpPointStoreRefusalMessage` do what it was written for; better, translate `details.vendorCode` into the sentence
   ("la ciudad no existe", "el número de la calle no existe" — the documented list is in the research note the comment
   cites), because that is what the operator has to change.
2. **Then make the code a type, not a convention.** `API_ERROR_CODES` and `ApiError['code']` are imported by **exactly
   one file** in the whole API (`all-exceptions.filter.ts:11,100-101`); nothing else constrains what a service may put in
   `code:`, which is why 106 undeclared codes, a table emitted from a mapper and a ternary all survived three censuses.
   Give the thrown payloads a typed factory (or an augmentation) so `code` must be a member of the contract's enum: every
   one of them becomes a **compile error**, and each call site is forced to make the choice §118.4 describes — declare
   it, or throw the declared generic one with the cause in `details`. That is the only version of this fix that does not
   depend on the hunt's next regex.

### 122.4 The rest of the Devices screen, checked and clean

The screen was picked because it consumes more endpoints than any other (six), and the checks that came back clean are
recorded so the sweep is not repeated:

| Check                               | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/kds/devices` → the screen's reads | every field it renders is in the adapter's shape — `device_id`, `device_name`, `station_id`/`station_name`, `last_used_at`, `ip`, `status` (`devices.jsx:212-238` against `toDeviceRow`, `kds.service.ts:1447-1465`)                                                                |
| Are the v1 reads reachable?         | yes — `getPosEnrollmentRequests`, `getPosDevices`, `getHardware` (`data.jsx:838-860`) are all called at `devices.jsx:194-196`, so the enrolment/hardware estate the screen shows is the real one (this was checked because nothing else in the dashboard mentions `v1/merchants`)   |
| `HARDWARE_CONNECTION_LABELS`        | **9 of 9** values of `hardware_device_connection_state_check` (`connected, disconnected, connecting, busy, recovering, failed, disabled, error, unknown`) — and the same map covers the narrower diagnostic set                                                                     |
| `HARDWARE_TRANSPORT_LABELS`         | **9 of 9** of `hardware_device_transport_check`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `POS_STATE_LABELS`                  | 8 of the CHECK's 9 — `approved` has no label, and the API never writes it (the approve path goes `awaiting_approval → credential_ready`, `devices.repository.ts:386,403,454`), so nothing renders a raw token. The unlabelled value is dead vocabulary of §102's kind, not a defect |
| `platformLabel` / `mobilityLabel`   | cover the CHECKs (`android/ios/linux/macos/windows/web`; `static/mobile`)                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The MP Point vendor-code path       | correct nesting, verified by reading: `details` is passed through for 4xx, `mpPointStoreRefusalCode` unwraps `err.details.error.details` (`device-utils.js:150-156`) — which is why §122.2 is about the _sentence_, not about the data                                              |

## 123. The Settings screen's Save writes eleven fields the endpoint strips, and answers 200 — while the screen's own comment says it wrote them somewhere else

**Severity: med-high (an owner's edits are accepted, displayed, and not stored).** Found 2026-10-09 by reading the
Settings screen the way §122 taught: what it _writes_, against what the route _accepts_.

### 123.1 One Save button, three requests, and one of them cannot land

`handleSave` fires three calls in `Promise.allSettled` (`settings.jsx:377-428`). Two of them are the shapes their routes
declare; the first is not:

| Call                                                                  | Route                                                                                                                  | Does the body match?       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `saveRewardConfig({rewardName, visitsRequired, rewardCostCentavos})`  | `PATCH …/cash/reward-config`                                                                                           | yes                        |
| `saveMerchantVoice({tone_preset, assistant_name, tone, style_notes})` | the voice route, whose service writes `merchant.merchant.assistant_name` / `assistant_tone` (`voice.service.ts:27-54`) | yes — **this half lands**  |
| `saveMerchantSettings({…})` — **14 keys**                             | `PATCH /api/merchants/:merchantId/settings` (`data.jsx:646-655`)                                                       | **no: the DTO declares 4** |

The DTO is `UpdateSettingsDto`: `name`, `timezone`, `businessDayStart`, `segmentThresholds` (`update-settings.dto.ts:46-69`,
the last one a nested class of five numbers). The screen sends fourteen keys, of which **three** are declared (`name`,
`businessDayStart`, `segmentThresholds`) and **eleven are not**: `city`, `primaryColor`, `secondaryColor`, `passStyle`,
`promoMessage`, `promoStartsAt`, `promoEndsAt`, `promoDays`, `selfRegistration`, `birthdayRewardEnabled`,
`birthdayRewardName`.

### 123.2 Why they vanish, and why nothing says so

The global pipe is `new ClassValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, transform: true })` (`main.ts:45`), and
`ClassValidationPipe` is a thin `extends ValidationPipe` (`class-validation.pipe.ts:22-27`) — so `whitelist` keeps its
meaning: **unknown properties are stripped, not refused**. The request therefore answers `200 {"ok":true}`
(`merchants.controller.ts:121-127`) while `updateMerchantSettings` writes the four keys it has.

Two things make this worse than a typo:

1. **The columns exist.** `merchant.merchant` carries `city`, `brand_color` and `secondary_color` (and
   `assistant_name`/`assistant_tone`, which the _voice_ half of the same Save does write). So this is not "there is
   nowhere to put it": it is a writer whose schema cannot reach its own table's columns.
2. **The screen's comment claims a different owner** (`settings.jsx:21-23`): _"Save: saveMerchantSettings(patch) →
   PATCH /api/[merchantRef]/admin/settings"_ — umi-cash's surface. The code posts to the API's route instead, and the
   _read_ path prefers umi-cash (`data.jsx:415-417`: `cashSettings?.primaryColor || s.primaryColor`). So the screen reads
   branding from one application and writes it to another whose schema refuses it — and the comment, describing the
   intent rather than the code, is why nobody noticed. (§21 already covers the related fact that this URL is one the
   contract's route table does not carry; this is the payload half of the same gap.)

### 123.3 The symptom an owner sees

`handleSave` re-bases its own state (`setBase({biz, seg, brand, loyalty, birthday, promo, selfReg})`, `:437-441`) and sets
`saved` for 2.5 s — and never refetches the merchant. So the new colours, promo banner and birthday reward **appear
immediately**, the screen says _Cambios guardados_, and the edit is gone on the next load, because the fresh read comes
from umi-cash (preferred) or from the API's settings (which never received it). An owner who trusts the confirmation and
reloads later sees their work undone, with no error anywhere to explain it.

### 123.4 Fix

1. **Give the fields an owner, once.** Either point `saveMerchantSettings` at umi-cash's admin settings — what the screen's
   comment already says the design is, and what the read path already prefers — or extend `UpdateSettingsDto` and
   `updateMerchantSettings` with the café-owned fields the API's own columns hold (`city`, `brandColor`, `secondaryColor`)
   and move the loyalty-ish ones (`promo*`, `selfRegistration`, `birthdayReward*`, `passStyle`) to the module that owns
   those tables. Both are decisions about ownership; neither is a bug fix on its own.
2. **Then make the drop loud.** `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` turns every one of these into a `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` the
   first time the button is pressed, which is the cheapest detector available and the one this hunt would have paid for.
3. **And add the check**: every body a screen sends must be reconciled with the request model declared for that route.
   Where the contract carries no request model (§21), the reconciliation has to come from the repository's DTO — which is
   exactly why §21's gap is not cosmetic: it removes the only place a screen's payload could have been compared to
   anything.

## 124. The kill switch exists — and it announces itself as a permission problem

**Severity: med (the operator is told to ask a manager for something no manager can grant).** Found 2026-10-09 while
checking §119's neighbours, and it **corrects §119's conclusion**: the platform _can_ switch a café off; it does it
through the product entitlement, and `merchant.status` is not a second door but a decorative label.

### 124.1 The mechanism that does work

`EntitlementGuard` (`auth/entitlement.guard.ts:14-45`) runs on **61** `@RequireProduct(…)` annotations across the API. It
reads the café's entitlement for that product and refuses unless the status is one of `PRODUCT_ACTIVE_STATUSES` —
`active`, `trialing` (`packages/contract/src/entitlements.ts:32-35`, ported 1:1 from the legacy `server.js`). The till's
own controllers carry `@RequireProduct('pos')` (`pos-cash.controller.ts:29`, `tender.controller.ts:31`,
`pos-cart.controller.ts:31`, `pos-order.controller.ts:24`, `table-map.controller.ts:34`), and POS PIN sign-in checks the
same entitlement (`auth.service.ts:331-334`). So switching the `pos` product off **does** stop the till — the platform has
a real kill switch, per product, enforced per request.

### 124.2 What that refusal looks like when it lands

There are two paths and they disagree about what to call it:

| Path                                                      | Payload                                                                          | What the client receives                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **At sign-in** — `auth.service.ts:331-334`                | `throw new ForbiddenException({ code: 'ENTITLEMENT_DISABLED' })`                 | the declared code, and the till has a sentence for it (`entry_surface.dart:328` → _"UmiPOS no está habilitado para este negocio."_) |
| **On every other request** — `entitlement.guard.ts:31-44` | `throw new ForbiddenException({ error: 'product_not_active', product, status })` | `403` with `code: PERMISSION_DENIED` and `message: "product_not_active"`                                                            |

The second is the one a _live_ session meets, and it is wrong twice over. `PRODUCT_NOT_ACTIVE` is declared nowhere
(checked) and named by no client (checked), and because the payload spells its key **`error:`** rather than `code:`, the
filter's builder finds no declared code and falls back (`all-exceptions.filter.ts:95-113`): `code = codeForStatus(403) =
'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, then `message` resolves to `source.error`, i.e. the literal string **`product_not_active`**. So the
till classifies it as `AppErrorCategory.permission` and the operator is told to get a manager's authorisation — for a
condition that a manager's PIN cannot change, because the product is off for the **business**, and the sentence that
says so already exists in the till's own strings.

### 124.3 Measured

| Measure                                                          | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `@RequireProduct(…)` annotations enforcing the gate              | **61**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `PRODUCT_NOT_ACTIVE` in the contract / named by any client       | **no / no**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ENTITLEMENT_DISABLED` in the contract / branched on by the till | **yes / yes — at sign-in only**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| umi-cash's own gate for comparison                               | `requireActiveSubscription` refuses **402 "Servicio suspendido"** on **10** of its 33 route handlers, and auto-suspends an expired trial (`lib/tenant.ts:119-149`), with `subscriptions.status` in **uppercase** (`SUSPENDED`) against this side's lowercase `active`/`trialing` — three suspension vocabularies across the two apps and the unread column of §119 |

### 124.4 Blind spot five, recorded

This refusal is emitted with the **`error:` spelling** — the very "two spellings" the dashboard's own comment documents
(`data.jsx:159-165`, _"the POS/operations routes throw `{ code: … }`, and a route that throws `{ error: … }` arrives as
`payload.error.error`"_). §118's and §120's censuses both extracted `code: 'LITERAL'`, so this one was invisible to
both — the fifth extraction blind spot in this family, after same-file accessors (§117.8), mapper tables (§121.4),
expressions (§122.1) and now the second key spelling. It is worth stating plainly, because it is also the shape of §119's
own near-miss: a census is only as wide as the shapes it knows.

### 124.5 Fix

1. **One name on both paths.** The guard throws the declared `ENTITLEMENT_DISABLED` (with `details: { product, status }`),
   so the in-session refusal reaches the sentence the till already has — and a client can tell "this product is off"
   apart from "you lack a permission", which today it cannot.
2. **Correct §119's honest half**: `merchant.merchant.status` is still read by nothing (§119 stands as a _dead column_
   and a dead contract pair), but the platform is not without a switch — so the fix for §119 is not "build suspension";
   it is "make `merchant.status` either the same door as the entitlement or say in the schema that it is not".

---

## 125. The other application, swept: umi-cash's 33 handlers, and the two admin surfaces compared route by route

**Severity: low (one gate inconsistency) + one spent lens and one new blind spot.** Measured 2026-10-09. §124 sent me into
umi-cash — the app that answers the _same_ `/api/{ref}/admin/*` URLs the dashboard calls — and this is the census of it.

### 125.1 The census, and what each apparent gap turned out to be

All **33** route handlers under `apps/umi-cash/src/app/api` were checked for four things: a staff/platform auth check, a
tenant check, the subscription gate, and a zod schema for the body.

| Apparent gap         | Count | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No `requireAuth(…)`  | 13    | **Five are the platform surface** and use their own gate: `verifyUmiSession` (a dedicated admin JWT with its own secret, `UMI_ADMIN_JWT_SECRET`, deliberately not the tenant secret — `umi/auth/route.ts:6-12`) on `umi/tenants`, `umi/tenants/[id]`, `umi/geocode`, `umi/auth`; and `isAuthorizedCron(authorization)` on `umi/push-passes`. The rest are public **by design**: `[slug]/auth/login | refresh | logout`, `[slug]/card/qr`(which does check a session — via`getAuthUser`, a helper my grep did not know), `[slug]/customers`(self-registration),`[slug]/gift/[code]`, `[slug]/passes/apple/v1/[...path]`(§22 read the one that matters), and`[slug]/stamp-strip/[state]` |
| No tenant check      | 4     | `auth/logout` (nothing to scope), plus the three platform handlers above                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| No subscription gate | 24    | Correct for reads, sign-in and the public pages; **the money paths all have it** — `admin/topup`, `admin/purchase`, `admin/gift-cards` (POST), `admin/scan`, `admin/scan/preview`, `admin/scan/seals`, `admin/redemptions/[id]/revert`, `admin/customers/[id]` (PATCH)                                                                                                                             |
| No zod               | 18    | Nine are GETs; `redemptions/[id]/revert` **takes no body at all** (verified by reading it: ADMIN-only, tenant, subscription, staff attribution, `lockCard` + re-read under the lock, ledger-preserving, wallet push after the response) — a zod schema would have nothing to validate                                                                                                              |

**`stamp-strip/[state]` deserves its own line** because it is anonymously reachable: it is a content-addressed stamp image
for Google Wallet's `heroImage`, and the file says why that is safe — the URL carries the tenant slug and counts, no PII,
the state is parsed and bounded (`parseStripState(params.state, MAX_REQUIRED=20)`), and the bytes for a given state never
change (`route.ts:11-24,29-31`). Clean.

### 125.2 The two admin surfaces, route by route

`CashController` in the API is mounted at `@Controller('api/:merchantRef/admin')` (`cash.controller.ts:85`) — **the same
URL space** umi-cash answers with `[slug]/admin/*`. Fourteen routes exist in both; umi-cash adds seven (`messages`,
`PATCH customers/:id`, `POST gift-cards`, `purchase`, `scan`, `scan/preview`, `scan/seals`, `topup`). For the ones in both,
the guards are equivalent:

| Concern                                                                      | API (`cash.controller.ts`)                                                                                                                                               | umi-cash                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Product / subscription                                                       | `@RequireProduct('cash')` at the class — every route gated by the entitlement                                                                                            | `requireActiveSubscription` on the eight money handlers, 402    |
| Sensitive reads (`customers`, `customers/:id`, `export`)                     | authenticated member through `UseGuards(AuthGuard, MerchantAccessGuard, EntitlementGuard, RolesGuard)`; the export rate-limited **per staff member** (`:37`, `:174-180`) | `requireAuth(['STAFF','ADMIN'])`, same 10-per-hour stance       |
| `POST redemptions/:id/revert`                                                | `@RequirePermission('merchant.manage')`; service fails closed on attribution, restores by tier, refuses a second revert (`cash-scan.service.ts:352-397`)                 | `requireAuth(['ADMIN'])`; same four properties, plus `lockCard` |
| The till's remaining reads (`stats`, `analytics`, `customers`, `gift-cards`) | open to a cashier **on purpose**, with the reason written above the class (`:78-81`)                                                                                     | `requireAuth(['STAFF','ADMIN'])`                                |

So the "two worlds" of §87/§88 are about the **data** (two gift-card tables, two loyalty ledgers), not the guards: on the
shared surface the two implementations agree on who may do what. Recorded so the sweep is not repeated.

### 125.3 The one asymmetry found

umi-cash gates its **money** handlers and not its **configuration** ones: `admin/settings` (PATCH), `admin/reward-config`
(PUT), `admin/reward-config/resync`, and the analytics/stats/customers/messages reads carry no subscription check. On the
API side the class-level `@RequireProduct('cash')` covers all of them, so the same café is _fully_ stopped in one
deployment and _half_ stopped in the other — suspended cafés can still edit the reward programme that will govern their
customers when they return. Severity of the inconsistency is low (config, not money), and the fix is one line per handler
if the intent is "suspended means read-only".

### 125.4 Blind spot six: the guard's name

This census keyed on `requireAuth`. umi-cash's own gates are three other names — `getAuthUser` (`card/qr`), `verifyUmiSession`
(the platform handlers) and `isAuthorizedCron` (`push-passes`) — so thirteen handlers _looked_ unauthenticated
until each was read. That is the sixth extraction blind spot in this hunt's families, after same-file accessors (§117.8),
mapper tables (§121.4), expressions (§122.1), the `error:` spelling (§124.4) and the `code:`/`error:` pair generally: a
census over _names_ is only as good as its list of names, and the fix that keeps mattering is the same — assert on the
**type** or on the **table**, not on a grep.
